The sequential format provided an integrated way to examine potential benefits, misuse risks, and real-world implementation challenges, rather than considering these issues in isolation. The exercise surfaced non-obvious misuse pathways, expanded potential interventions beyond purely technical safeguards, and highlighted operational and policy constraints that could affect implementation. This report summarizes the workshop design, outputs, and lessons learned for applying violet teaming to the evaluation of complex, dual-use technologies.

title: Density-Guided Bootstrap Boundaries for Latent World-Model Reinforcement Learning
authors: Shashank Gupta, Pilhwa Lee
abstract: Latent world models allow reinforcement learning agents to learn policies from imagined trajectories, yet determining the optimal depth of model reliance remains a fundamental challenge. Fixed imagination horizons apply uniform prediction depths regardless of trajectory reliability, exposing target values to compounding model error or over-relying on critic approximations. We introduce density-guided bootstrap boundaries, a trajectory-dependent mechanism that adapts the depth of imagined returns using a score-informed relative density proxy. The proxy accumulates the estimated divergence of a score-corrected auxiliary field formed by a feature displacement network and a noise-conditioned score estimator along imagined paths. We propose two gating mechanisms: a hard boundary that halts return expansion at a discrete state, and a soft boundary that continuously shifts the return recursion toward critic bootstrapping. Both variants preserve boundary value estimates and apply corresponding survival weights to actor and critic losses. Formulated independently of specific dynamics models and instantiated within Dreamer V3, we prove that the resulting gated Bellman operator is a strict contraction mapping and that early bootstrapping monotonically reduces conditional target variance. We clarify the theoretical assumptions distinguishing our expansion proxy from exact path likelihoods. Across continuous-control tasks and Atari Pong, empirical evaluations show that dynamic boundary selection enhances sample efficiency and late-training performance over fixed-horizon and auxiliary-enabled baselines.

title: Omniprediction for All Mixable Proper Losses and Beyond
authors: Junyan Liu, Haipeng Luo, Lillian J. Ratliff
abstract:
Omniprediction concerns the task of making predictions that are simultaneously accurate with respect to different losses. Earlier results by [CV09] show that in an online learning setting, $O(\log(|\mathcal{F}||\mathcal{L}|))$ regret is achievable simultaneously against every predictor in a finite predictor class $\mathcal{F}$ and for every loss in a finite class $\mathcal{L}$ of mixable proper losses, while recent advances [OKK25, FP26] show that $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{T\log(|\mathcal{F}||\mathcal{L}|)})$ regret is achievable simultaneously for every loss in a finite class $\mathcal{L}$ of bounded losses.
  In this work, we ask whether sublinear regret remains possible when $\mathcal{L}$ is an infinite class of proper losses. Our first result gives a negative answer in general: even when $\mathcal{F}$ contains only two linear predictors, it is impossible to achieve sublinear regret simultaneously for all bounded proper losses. We then show that $\widetilde{O}(T^{1/3}(\log|\mathcal{F}|)^{2/3})$ regret is achievable simultaneously for \textit{all} mixable proper losses and that this bound is optimal up to logarithmic factors. This optimal rate stands in stark contrast to the constant (in $T$) regret achievable for a finite class of mixable proper losses. Finally, we extend our algorithm to obtain a best-of-all-worlds result: in addition to the new regret guarantee for all mixable proper losses, the resulting algorithm simultaneously achieves the existing guarantees for finite loss classes. With appropriate choices of these finite classes, our algorithm simultaneously achieves constant regret for squared loss and log loss, $\widetilde{O}(T^{1/3}(\log|\mathcal{F}|)^{2/3})$ regret for all mixable proper losses, and $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{T\log|\mathcal{F}|})$ regret for $0$-$1$ loss, all Lipschitz losses, all GLM losses, and other structured families.

title: Dreams Are Cheaper Than Flights: Curated World-Model Data Improves Aerial Detection
authors: Rugved Katole, Vedant Patil, Jenna Kline, Christopher Stewart
abstract: Robot perception is increasingly data driven, yet field data is slow, costly, and sometimes disruptive to collect. Video world models offer a cheaper source: seeded with real frames, they extend a recorded scene into new footage with the deployment's sensor, altitude, and environment. We ask whether such synthetic data matches the utility of real field data and whether detectors trained with it perform in the field. Seeding a 7B-parameter world model with wildlife drone video, we more than double the training set with curated frames. On held-out videos from the same drones, mAP@50--95 rises 4.3\% when these frames are added to real data and 10.3\% when they replace it, and up to 33.5\% on an urban benchmark. Although an expert rejects an estimated 87.5\% of generated clips, the data costs about \$1,100 of GPU time, against more than \$3,200 of field labor alone for a less useful real training set. Synthetic data thus shifts data costs from fieldwork to compute.

title: Contact Imitation Interface: Transferring Dexterous Skills by Showing How Contact Unfolds
authors: Zhixuan Xu, Yichen Li, Bingchen Wu, Rui Wang, Yiwen Hou, Zixuan Liu, Tianyu Qiu, Lin Shao
abstract: Robot-free human demonstrations offer a promising route to scaling dexterous manipulation data. The key challenge is to preserve the demonstrator's natural dexterity while producing contact-grounded observations and actions that transfer to robot hands. We present Contact Imitation Interface (CIMI), a framework with contact-grounded demonstration and learning interfaces. The demonstration interface combines shared contact geometry and fingertip RGB views with contact-alignment-first retargeting and reprojection of wider scene views. The learning interface introduces a hierarchical policy in which a contact-surface planner predicts relative contact-surface trajectories and a controller coordinates wrist and finger commands to improve contact alignment. CIMI combines contact-grounded observations, retargeting, and action representations, improving mean final-stage success by at least 50 percentage points over baseline policies across six hand-task pairs on LEAP and Wuji. Hardware designs and software are publicly available.
comment: 15 pages (8-page main paper and 7-page supplementary material). Project website with code and hardware designs: https://nus-lins-lab.github.io/CIMIWeb/

title: ReplayRCA: Measuring Post-hoc Diagnosis and Live Oversight of Agent Failures by Counterfactual Replay
authors: Jeremy Canale, Fabien Soulis
abstract: When a language-model agent fails a multi-step task, can another model find the decisive mistake and fix it with a single action? We introduce ReplayRCA, a benchmark that scores such diagnoses by intervention rather than by agreement with annotations: the environment is restored to the state preceding the chosen step, the proposed action replaces the agent's own, and the same agent continues. The score, causal repair, is the continuation success rate minus that of a paired placebo that replays the agent's original action through the same mechanism. Two tracks share this protocol: a post-hoc autopsy, where the diagnoser sees the whole failed run and is told that it failed, and live oversight, where a supervisor watches the run unfold and may intervene once, before an irreversible action, without knowing whether the run will fail. Tasks come from OpsWorld, a deterministic, procedurally generated back-office environment with six difficulty levels, the last of which is multimodal (QR codes, handwriting). On 62 calibrated systematic failures, the best of 13 frontier models (Grok 4.7) reaches a causal repair of +51.3 points; the top eight models are statistically indistinguishable, the flagship models of the two largest vendors rank 8th and 12th, and 5 items are repaired by no model. Forcing a strong model to intervene at the last step costs it 17.1 points, so the last-step shortcut of annotation-based attribution benchmarks does not transfer. On 87 runs, the two best live supervisors are statistically tied and one of them is a small open-weight model (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash); the supervisor that is among the best post-hoc diagnosers (GPT-6.1 Sol) is the weakest live one (-14.5 points on the same runs, p = 0.002), so post-hoc diagnostic performance can be a poor proxy for live oversight. The environment and the evaluation code are released at https://github.com/jeremy1392/RCAreplay.

title: Privacy-Constrained Function Computation in Distributed Databases
authors: Vamoua Yachongka, Rémi A. Chou
abstract: Consider distributed databases that contain both sensitive (private) and non-sensitive (public) attributes. A user seeks to compute a function of public attributes and side information by interacting with the databases and downloading their responses. In this paper, we study the trade-offs among download cost, information leakage about the private attributes, and distortion between the computed function and its reconstruction, referred to as the capacity region. Our main contributions are as follows. For a single database, we provide a complete characterization of the capacity region for general discrete sources and characterize the capacity region of two different setups for Gaussian sources when the computed function is defined as the sum of the public attribute and side information. For distributed databases, we establish inner and outer bounds on the capacity region of discrete sources and we characterize the capacity region when the databases and the side information are mutually independent. As a special instance, we study lossless function computation, and results analogous to the lossy case are obtained.
comment: A preliminary version of this paper was presented at IEEE ISIT 2025

title: An Incentive-Aligned Trust-Centric Coordination Layer for Heterogeneous Blockchain Interoperability
authors: Saeed Moradi, Sara Rouhani
abstract: The interoperability between permissioned and public blockchains is hampered by asymmetric privacy, trust, and governance assumptions. We propose a coordination architecture that decouples cross-domain trust management and privacy enforcement from underlying blockchain protocols, requiring no protocol-level modifications. The framework integrates cryptographic unlinkability mechanisms with incentive-compatible relay selection, combining stake-weighted participation and temporally accumulated reputation to align economic commitment with sustained correctness. We formalize the adversarial model and derive security and privacy properties for cross-domain coordination, demonstrating robustness against Sybil infiltration, collusion, and strategic stake concentration. Simulation-based analysis characterizes key design trade-offs between quorum thresholds, reputation memory, and anonymity parameters, indicating that privacy-preserving coordination can be achieved without degrading responsiveness or incentive stability when parameters are properly tuned.

title: WebOverlay: High-Throughput Vision-Only Distillation for Extreme Aspect-Ratio Web Overlay Detection
authors: Jiannan Huang, Jerry Ding, Li Yu, Zhenting Li
abstract: Web overlays, such as cookie consent banners, newsletter prompts, and age gates, obstruct automated web crawlers and degrade downstream document representations. While proprietary multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) can accurately identify overlays, their latency and inference cost preclude web-scale ingestion. Conversely, lightweight vision models struggle with full-page renderings characterized by extreme vertical aspect ratios, where standard isotropic resizing collapses critical text features and causes false positives. In this work, we present WebOverlay, a high-throughput vision-only detector trained via distillation from a frontier vision-language teacher. We establish a dynamic tiling strategy that partitions extreme aspect-ratio web renders into aspect-preserving patches with spatial overlap, coupled with an aspect-ratio-aware boundary adjudication mechanism to eliminate boundary artifacts. To eliminate cross-modal latency overheads, our student model relies purely on visual cues, bypassing DOM tree parsing. WebOverlay significantly outperforms DOM-based heuristics and achieves competitive precision and recall against heavy proprietary MLLM baselines while delivering multiple orders of magnitude higher throughput and substantially reduced deployment costs.

title: When can Optimally Trained Transformers Achieve Near-Lossless Token Prediction for non-Markovian Data?
authors: Kağan Akman, Jake Feldman Starosta, Naci Saldi, Serdar Yüksel
abstract: There exists little mathematical theory explaining why Transformer architectures are empirically successful even for non-Markovian data. To this end, this paper studies next-token prediction via stochastic optimal control theoretically trained Transformers for such sources, where we consider either stationary and ergodic non-Markovian sources or those which are hidden Markov models of some finite order (possibly non-stationary). In either case, we first obtain error bounds via finite models with finite window approximations. For stationary ergodic sources, the resulting error is bounded by an entropy gap; for $N$th order Markovian sources, it decays at an exponential rate $α^{\lfloor M/N\rfloor}$, where $M$ is the window length and $α$ is determined by filter stability (and the Dobrushin coefficients of the transition and measurement kernels). We then construct a Transformer of depth $M+1$, one head per layer, realizing the truncated filter, and we optimally train it with stochastic control developed in earlier work, which rigorously returns a near optimal Transformer. In particular, we show that for a non-Markovian source, either under stationarity and ergodicity for general models or under filter stability for hidden Markov models, an optimally trained Transformer has arbitrarily small performance error with increasing context length, data, and approximation refinement. Numerical studies accompany the theory.

title: Before We Adapt: The Zero-Shot Generalization Bottleneck in Continual World Models
authors: Amir Mesbah, Di Wu
abstract: Continual reinforcement learning (CRL) requires agents to operate under environmental changes while reusing prior knowledge whenever possible. We argue that model-based reinforcement learning provides a promising framework for this setting because learned world models (WMs) can, in principle, support change detection, knowledge reuse, adaptation, and acquisition of new knowledge. However, such benefits depend heavily on whether the learned model can generalize beyond the contexts in which it was trained. In this work, we propose to formulate this problem with a contextual Markov decision process in which context is decomposed into behavioral and physical components. This view organizes continual WM learning into reuse, adaptation, and acquisition of new knowledge. As a first step, we study direct reuse when behavioral rules remain unchanged. Using Dyna-Q and TD-MPC in controlled FourRooms tasks, we find that zero-shot reuse can degrade substantially under physical-context changes and that this behavior depends strongly on the observation representation used by the WM. Additional ablation studies and latent-space diagnostics suggest that learned representations do not automatically provide the invariances needed for reuse. These results identify representation generalization as an important bottleneck for reliable world-model reuse in CRL.
comment: Accepted to Continual World Models workshop @ NeurIPS 2026

title: Characterizing Recoverable Expert-Utilization Signatures in Fine-Tuned Mixture-of-Experts LLMs
authors: Fei Wang, Baochun Li, Bo Li
abstract:
As Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) large language models are increasingly deployed in distributed environments, from federated learning to edge-cloud systems, their architecture harbors an underexplored landscape of security vulnerabilities. Moving beyond textual analysis, we uncover structural memorization: a novel vulnerability where a fine-tuned model memorizes not only its training data but also the internal pathway used to process it, creating a characteristic routing fingerprint unique to the training process. We provide comprehensive empirical evidence that structural memorization emerges consistently even from a few samples, and that its intensity is directly influenced by the choice of trainable modules.
  We show that these memorized expert pathways can be stealthily recovered through the model's unconditional generation, using only routing and output logits, with no knowledge of the fine-tuning data or procedure. In distributed deployments, this vulnerability is amplified as routing information is exposed at multiple trust boundaries, including federated aggregation points, edge-cloud interfaces, and multi-tenant monitoring systems. Recovery exposes a critical blind spot: traditional membership inference metrics, viewed through the lens of expert routing, fail to identify memorized data corresponding to these structural pathways. To close this gap, we devise composite metrics combining reference model tail likelihood with complexity-aware normalization, significantly improving detection of memorized routing structures. This enables adversaries to pinpoint critical experts shaped by fine-tuning, whether dominant or dormant, and execute targeted attacks such as router manipulation or backdoor injection in realistic distributed settings where attackers lack training data but can observe routing patterns across system components.

title: Capability-Grounded Agentic Planning
authors: Shikha Shrestha, William Yeoh, Ning Zhang, Yevgeniy Vorobeychik
abstract: LLM agents serve natural-language requests through tools, data sources, and other agents, and even simple requests often need several interdependent calls. Typically, the LLM picks these calls by trial and error, with no guarantee of an executable plan. We present Capability-Grounded Agentic Planning (CGAP), which instead reasons about what a request requires and what tools provide. CGAP compiles the tool catalog deterministically into a PDDL model, uses an LLM to turn the request into goals, and solves the model with a classical planner. Since tool outputs are unknown in advance, the model is abstract, tracking which inputs are available, not their values. During execution, an LLM adds entity-specific calls that abstract plans omit, and deterministic checks reject any that break the plan. Every argument is drawn from a cited source, such as a conversation span or an earlier tool response, and each requested result counts as delivered only after an LLM verifier checks it against the request. With three LLMs on ToolSandbox, ComplexFuncBench, BFCL multi-turn, and $τ^2$-bench retail, CGAP outperforms a standard tool-calling agent by up to 28.9 points.

title: Meshless Latent Dynamics Models for Model Order Reduction of time-dependent Partial Differential Equations
authors: Lorenzo Tomada, Federico Pichi, Gianluigi Rozza
abstract:
Latent dynamics learning has emerged as a prominent approach for Model Order Reduction (MOR) of time-dependent, parameterized Partial Differential Equations (PDEs). Traditional autoencoder-based approaches are intrinsically tied to fixed spatial discretizations during both training and inference, motivating the development of meshless methodologies. In this context, conditioning provides a natural mechanism for representing temporal evolution through spatially continuous functions, enabling mesh-agnostic Latent Dynamics Models (LDMs).
  In this work, we introduce a unified mathematical framework for mesh-agnostic LDMs based on conditioning in Neural Fields (NeFs). Leveraging a taxonomy of conditioning mechanisms (weak, strong, and pure), we formulate meshless LDMs as NeFs conditioned on a latent state. We establish a Universal Approximation Theorem (UAT) for this class of models and analyze their stability by deriving Lipschitz bounds for different conditioning mechanisms. Our analysis reveals an expressivity--stability trade-off, providing insight into why more expressive conditioning, despite its higher representational capacity, can potentially degrade performance during temporal extrapolation. Finally, we provide a comprehensive comparison of meshless and mesh-based architectures in the continuous limit of the spatial discretization, showing that meshless models guarantee grid-independent Lipschitz bounds, unlike mesh-based counterparts.
  Our experiments across Burgers' equation, Navier--Stokes flow past a cylinder, and linear advection show that meshless LDMs can achieve predictive accuracy comparable to or better than their mesh-based counterparts while using only 2% of the trainable parameters and exhibiting nearly constant error across spatial discretizations.

title: Consensus Within, Competition Between: Decentralized LLM Teams for Perimeter Defense
authors: Khawaja Abaid Ullah, Ananya Acharya, Mohammad Javad Khojasteh
abstract: The use of large language models (LLMs) to coordinate multi-agent teams raises a fundamental architectural question: whether task allocation should be centralized in a single LLM controller or distributed across autonomous LLM agents, particularly when communication is unreliable. In a deliberately simplified perimeter-defense simulation against LLM-controlled intruders, we compared a central commander, an auction-based consensus team and independent agents under five network conditions. Breach rates were 15% for the consensus team, 32% for the commander and 29% for independent agents, and of the different network conditions, only limited radio range changed a team's breach rate, raising the commander's. In consensus team, giving a low-cost LLM more authority over the bid computation raised breaches by 38 percentage points. With birds and civilian drones in airspace, we added a photograph for each to the input text state. Only the near-frontier model treated them apart from intruders. Intruders disguised as existing taxidermy bird drones were mistook as birds by both low-cost and near-frontier LLMs, going unpursued in 59-61% of near-frontier decisions (1-16% before). However, a one-sentence forewarning in the prompt lowered it to 0-25%. We find that LLM team with a dedicated external conflict resolution protocol results in fewest breaches. Code: https://github.com/the-kas-lab/consensus-within-competition-between.
comment: 88 pages (33 main text and references, 55 supplementary material), 7 main figures. Code: https://github.com/the-kas-lab/consensus-within-competition-between

title: Localizing predictive concepts encoded in neural representations via hierarchical testing
authors: Viktoriia Huryn, Marco Simnacher, Jim Berend, Wojciech Samek, Christoph Lippert, Sonja Greven, Uwe Ohler
abstract: Understanding which regulatory sequence motifs a genomic deep learning model has learned, with statistical error guarantees, is essential for trusting its use in downstream tasks such as variant effect prediction. Existing approaches to identifying which units in a trained network encode human- understandable concepts fall into two groups. Exploratory methods rank and visualize units but offer no statistical guarantee that the selected units are associated with the prediction target across the population of inputs. Testing-based methods test only single units or one pre-defined set of them, and do not control the error across the many sets of units. We introduce CUTTIE (Cluster-tree Unit Top-down Testing of Independence with Error control), which clusters the units of each layer into a tree and tests the clusters top-down with conditional independence tests, localizing information about the target while controlling the family-wise error rate. Thereby, we identify clusters that carry information about the target beyond the rest of the layer. For the units in the identified clusters, conditional attribution maps then reveal what motifs they encode. In a controlled simulation, the procedure identifies the clusters whose concepts affect the target. We apply the procedure to a convolutional model predicting cell-type-specific chromatin accessibility from DNA sequence, where the concepts encoded in the identified clusters map onto known regulatory motifs.

title: Measuring Personal Information Exposure in Mental Health-Related Conversations with LLMs
authors: Synthia Qia Wang, Ranya Sharma, Christine Lee, Sarah Keedy, Marshini Chetty, Nick Feamster
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for informal mental health support, yet the privacy implications of conversational interaction remain poorly understood. Prior LLM privacy research has focused largely on model-side risks such as memorization and adversarial extraction, leaving personal information inferred from ordinary conversation understudied. We introduce a profile-recovery framework that measures personal information exposure by comparing user profiles with attributes inferred from conversation alone. We generate 240 synthetic multi-turn mental health conversations from profiles sampled from a nationally representative health survey and validate them against real counseling transcripts, finding comparable overall disclosure volume. Across 21 attributes, 33-41% of each profile is recoverable, with 76.5% first-inference and 94.3% any-of-3 accuracy. 239 of 240 conversations expose at least one sensitive mental health attribute, and 45.0\% expose all six. Our findings reveal a gap between disclosure and inferability, motivating HCI approaches to make inference risks legible and support privacy-aware interaction design.

title: Faster #PPM from faster #3SAT
authors: László Kozma
abstract:
The counting variant (#PPM) of the permutation pattern matching (PPM) problem asks for the number of occurrences of a permutation pattern in a host permutation of length $n$. The problem admits faster algorithms than the trivial $O^*(2^n)$ time enumeration; the best known running time, for both PPM and #PPM, is $O(1.415^n)$ (Gawrychowski and Rzepecki). It is also known that PPM is ETH-hard: an algorithm with running time $2^{o(n/\log{n})}$ would imply a subexponential algorithm for 3SAT (Jelínek, Opler, and Pekárek).
  We give a reduction in the opposite direction, showing that an algorithm for counting satisfying assignments of a 3-CNF formula (#3SAT) in time $2^{O({n}/{f(n)})}$, where $n$ is the number of variables, yields an algorithm for #PPM with running time $2^{O({n \sqrt{\log{f(n)}/{f(n)}}})}$. In particular, the recently claimed refutation of ETH by OpenAI implies a #3SAT algorithm with an improvement factor $f(n) \in Ω(\sqrt{\log{n}}/\log\log{n})$ in the exponent; this yields, through our reduction, a subexponential algorithm for #PPM.

title: A System Dynamics Model for Zero-emission Heavy Vehicle Transition in Australia
authors: Elnaz Irannezhad, Seyed Hossein Hosseini, David A. Hensher
abstract: What would it take to accelerate the adoption of zero-emission trucks? Even if battery electric trucks become cheaper to own over their lifetime than diesel trucks, that alone is not enough. This study develops a system dynamics model of rigid and articulated truck fleets, calibrated to Australian fleets. Under current policy regimes, more than a third of the fleet still runs on diesel in 2050. Battery and fuel cell trucks become as attractive as diesel trucks only in 2031-2032, held back by slow fleet turnover and by how long operators take to trust the charging network, the most influential assumption tested in this study. Taxing diesel barely works at politically feasible levels. Charging trucks the full fuel excise lifts the zero-emission share by one percentage point; adding ten points would require a road user charge of about 5 AUD per litre, fifteen times the 2025-26 rate. A 70 AUD per tonne carbon price and a purchase subsidy covering 60% of the price premium do little better. Per percentage change in cost, operating-cost support is five to six times as effective as purchase support, yet the best single instrument adds only two percentage points. Only a combined push-pull package, which still raises fuel-tax revenue, shifts the market materially. Policy should stop relying on diesel prices and instead build operators' confidence in the network, cut operating costs and recycle road-charge revenue into infrastructure.

title: Closing the Applied Cybersecurity Gap in Critical Infrastructure: A Cyber-to-Physical Security Assessment Framework for Water Systems
authors: Halil Dursunoglu, Kaan Sulkalar
abstract: The integration of information technology and operational technology in water infrastructure creates pathways through which cyber compromise may affect physical service delivery. This study revisits the Applied Cybersecurity Gap (ACG) framework by evaluating an experimental Applied Cybersecurity Gap Index (ACGI) alongside the Cyber-to-Physical Propagation Rate (CPPR), defined as the proportion of initially compromised trials that produce a specified physical-impact outcome. The expanded evaluation comprises 2,160 synthetic trials across three water-network benchmarks, including EPANET Example Network 3 (Net3), and couples declared cyber-attack progression rules with hydraulic simulations. A source-trained machine-learning model evaluated on 247 compromised Net3 trials achieved ROC-AUC 0.772, PR-AUC 0.775, and F1 0.733, compared with 0.661, 0.642, and 0.704 for a scenario-only baseline. The configuration-cluster bootstrap interval for the ROC-AUC difference was 0.038--0.183. A separate 720-run Net3 hydraulic operating-point sensitivity analysis achieved the study's exploratory baseline pressure criterion in all reruns, preserved 717 of 720 physical-impact labels, and produced ROC-AUC 0.791 with the frozen source-trained model. Additional analyses examine the sensitivity of CPPR to the physical-impact threshold and assumed control-blocking probabilities, and demonstrate that the ACGI--CPPR association is partly induced by the simulation design rather than independently validated. The findings establish a reproducible simulation-based assessment workflow, but do not constitute field calibration of cybersecurity-control effectiveness or prediction of real-world utility incidents.

title: Veloxity: Towards Memory-Safe UAV Embedded Firmware using the Rust Programming Language
authors: Derek Ward, Brian Bascom, Tyler Larsen, James Usevitch, Phil Tokumaru, Tim McLain
abstract: Recent years have witnessed increased momentum towards memory-safe programming languages for safety-critical systems. Memory-safe languages can eliminate entire classes of common software errors that have historically required extensive analysis and expenditure to avoid. Nevertheless, memory-safe language adoption in aerospace remains fragmented and incomplete, particularly for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). Recent Rust UAV projects either run only in simulation, are closed source, or have not been integrated with an established autonomy ecosystem and tested against existing C/C++ firmware. To address this gap, we present Veloxity: an open-source embedded UAV autopilot written in the memory-safe Rust programming language. Veloxity lowers the barrier to using memory-safe languages within modern ecosystems by providing a minimal, modular foundation for autonomous UAVs. We compare Veloxity to equivalent autopilots written in C++ in simulation, with hardware testbenches, and via outdoor waypoint-following flight tests, demonstrating functional parity with improved performance. These results indicate that modern memory-safe languages are a viable option for reliable and performant firmware for autonomous aerospace systems.

title: Accept Changes, Reject Attacks: Robust Memory Management for LLM Agents
authors: Runze Zhao, Dongruo Zhou, Sumit Kumar Jha, Nathaniel D. Bastian, Ankit Shah
abstract: Since large language model (LLM) agents rely on long-term memory, what they store now shapes what they do later. A memory manager decides how each input changes this memory and which records the agent acts on. It can fail in two ways: keeping a fact that has since changed (outdated memory), or storing a planted passage or injected instruction (memory poisoning). Most prior work studies them separately, yet they call for opposite write decisions, so no fixed write rule handles both. We therefore formalize memory robustness as handling both without doing worse on other inputs. Since accuracy checks only the answer, we measure robustness with evidence-conditioned accuracy (ECA), which also checks that the records the manager selects include all the evidence the answer needs, updated and free of attacks. However, existing memory systems and defenses are not more robust than an untuned manager on our test sets. We improve robustness with a simple one-shot recipe that fine-tunes the manager on episodes synthesized around a single conversation with inserted changes and attacks. On three backbones, it improves every category score on our test sets and more than doubles the untuned manager's overall ECA, though robustness remains incomplete.

title: Nonlinear Maps Between Irreducible Representations in Graph Neural Networks
authors: Mani Shayestehfar
abstract: Equivariant linear maps cannot mix non-isomorphic irreducible representations, whereas nonlinear activations can. We develop a degree-resolved version of this nonlinear interaction picture and use the resulting block inventory to construct Specht Triple, a residual on unordered graph triples. On a synthetic structural benchmark with a frozen GIN backbone, Specht Triple reduces aggregate standardised test MSE by 11.05% relative to a parameter-matched Projector Control using the same irreducible projectors and complete linear equivariant space. The results support irreducible decomposition as an inductive bias for nonlinear higher-order equivariant processing.

title: Communication-Efficient Private Federated Reinforcement Learning with Post-Quantum Authentication for Vehicular Networks
authors: Hojat Allah Salehi, Devrim Aras, Md Jueal Mia, M. Hadi Amini, Imtiaz Karim, Mashrur Chowdhury, Bhavani Thuraisingham
abstract: Federated reinforcement learning supports cooperative vehicular routing without centralizing trajectory data, but model updates may reveal private information and incur communication overhead over intermittent vehicle-to-infrastructure links, particularly when post-quantum authentication is required. We study correlated private quantization, using complementary shared randomness between paired vehicles to reduce aggregation mean squared error while preserving the marginal parameter-level local differential privacy and one-bit communication cost of independent quantization. A tunable extension mixes shared and independent randomness to bound privacy leakage given paired outputs and shared-randomness side information. For this extension, Rényi differential privacy accounting establishes vector-level local differential privacy for one model upload even when pairings are revealed. Under matched vector-level privacy and identical local and global parameters, the extension yields 16.5% lower analytical aggregation mean squared error than independent quantization. We evaluate cooperative routing by coupling traffic simulation with packet-level simulation of post-quantum-authenticated vehicle-to-infrastructure communication. Compared to full-precision updates, one-bit uploads reduce authenticated uplink size by 92.4% and increase mean verified updates aggregated per round from 19.6 to 26.5. Under mobility-constrained communication at a parameter-level privacy budget of 1, correlated private quantization reduces mean travel time by 14.3% relative to independent quantization at the same budget and communication cost. At a parameter-level privacy budget of 0.3, a vehicle-origin inference attack trained on independent simulations reaches 30% accuracy with correlated private quantization and 22% with independent quantization after 100 rounds, versus 91% without privacy and 10% for random guessing.

title: Out of sync: Accommodation, evaluation, and emergence in five weeks with an agentic AI teammate
authors: Nia Nixon, Jaeyoon Choi, Pedro Martins de Bastos, Mohammad Amin Samadi
abstract: As agentic AI in education shifts from reactive tools toward partners that take initiative and persist over time, a central question is how learners relate to, evaluate, and benefit from artificial agency. We conducted a longitudinal experiment in an undergraduate learning analytics course, in which 17 student teams (N = 48) collaborated with a persistent LLM-based teammate across weekly sessions. The agent decided when to intervene through a trigger-based architecture, and its social role was manipulated between teams: a Cognitive Agent that challenged quick consensus or a Supportive Agent that invited quieter members to contribute. Combining chat discourse, post-session surveys, and spoken reflections, we identified distinct patterns unfolding across three timescales. Students accommodated their language to the agent's role immediately, using more social language toward the Supportive Agent from the first session. Their helpfulness evaluations were recalibrated from session to session in relation to the agent's observed behavior, rather than remaining anchored to students' pre-existing attitudes toward AI. A slower crossover emerged in perceived collaboration process and positive-affect word use in reflections: Supportive-Agent teams began below Cognitive-Agent teams and ended above them, although students rated the Supportive Agent less helpful throughout. Because these responses follow different trajectories, single-session evaluations of agentic AI may miss changes that emerge only through repeated interaction.
comment: 21 pages, 5 figures. Submitted to British Journal of Educational Technology

title: Single-Annotation, Multi-Hypothesis Segmentation with Semantic-Spatial Residual Banks
authors: Armin Dadras, Robert Sablatnig, Franziska Proksa, Markus Seidl
abstract: Multi-rater segmentation datasets show that a single image can admit several valid masks, yet most training sets expose only one annotation per image. We study single-annotation multi-hypothesis segmentation: each training image exposes one fixed mask, while the model must return a finite bank that covers held-out human annotations at test time. Our experiments reveal a representation tradeoff. Banks learned directly from images recover variations in local boundaries and extent but lose structural hypotheses, whereas frozen semantic features preserve structural grouping but underrepresent spatial variation. We introduce the Semantic-Spatial Residual Bank (SSRB), which freezes a semantic bank trained with balanced assignments and learns a residual from the image for each hypothesis. Across five medical endpoints, SSRB improves coverage of held-out masks at $K=8$ over a Probabilistic U-Net under the same one-mask constraint. On LIDC and LIDC-hard, it also produces substantially more distinct useful masks. On BSDS, it preserves the semantic bank's performance in grouping regions. Its advantage grows as more masks are returned, showing that residuals learned for corresponding heads improve coverage of local annotation variation while preserving how regions are grouped.

title: LanG 2.0: Energy-Efficient Agentic AI for Semi-Automated Security Operations at Scale
authors: Anes Abdennebi, Nadjia Kara, Laaziz Lahlou, Hakima Ould-Slimane
abstract: Security operations centers (SOCs) need to turn terabytes of alerts, logs and flows into trusted, affordable decisions to unveil hidden threats. We present LanG 2.0, an agentic system that detects threats, correlates evidence and writes rules, investigating whether small local models can replace frontier models affordably and safely when structural safeguards, not model accuracy, provide the guarantees. It incorporates entity-anchored correlation, human approval of rule changes and a tamper-evident ledger. Tests span eight flow datasets from five networks, real XDR alerts and multistage campaigns. Against its predecessor, campaign correlation precision rises from 18.75% to 51.81%, and rule acceptance from at most 60.00% to 98.33%. Against Claude Opus 5.5, scoring flows against each network's normal traffic detects attacks on unseen networks at 73.42% F1 without false positives, versus 58.10% with 49.00% false positives, for at least 650 times less energy. Finetuned models statistically match it on alert classification and rule writing for 5.6 to 59 times less energy. The work demonstrates LanG's practical scalability, processing 3.33 million records in 6.4 minutes, over 30 million hourly, and its safeguards resisted prompt injection, label poisoning and ledger tampering, so small local models can carry most SOC detection affordably and safely.

title: Segment Anything Pancreas: A Unified MRI Segmentation Model for Pancreatic Cancer Radiotherapy
authors: Zach Eidex, Mojtaba Safari, Kundan Thind, Parag J. Parikh, Zhen Tian, Xiaofeng Yang
abstract: Background: Limited tumor annotations and incomplete labels across MRI datasets hinder unified segmentation of pancreatic tumors and organs at risk (OARs) for MRI-guided radiotherapy. Purpose: We propose Pancreas-MedNeXt, a unified model that segments the whole pancreas, its subregions, tumors, and surrounding OARs from one MRI volume. Methods: The model uses a shared MedNeXt encoder-decoder with supervised whole-pancreas and subregion pretraining, followed by multitask fine-tuning. Three output heads predict the pancreatic subregions, tumor, and OARs (stomach, duodenum, kidneys). An annotation-aware loss allows training on partially labeled data without treating unannotated structures as background. Pancreas and tumor were evaluated by three-fold cross-validation on 142 PANTHER patients (92 diagnostic, 50 MR-Linac), subregions and OARs on Cyst-X and AMOS test sets, and pancreas and OARs on 33 external T1-weighted TotalSegmentator scans. Comparisons with nnU-Net, MedNeXt, VISTA3D, and Swin UNETR used the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) with paired bootstrap 95% CIs. Results: Pancreas-MedNeXt achieved the highest mean pancreas and tumor DSC on diagnostic and MR-Linac MRI. Tumor DSC was 58.41% and 42.55%, exceeding task-specific MedNeXt by 4.94 (95% CI: 0.28-9.45) and 5.89 (95% CI: 2.37-9.72) percentage points, respectively. Whole-pancreas DSC was 85.73% and 70.66%. Pretraining improved head, body, and tail DSC by 2.01, 3.00, and 3.78 percentage points over training from scratch. It also achieved the highest DSC for the pancreas, duodenum, and right kidney on AMOS, and for all five organs on external MRI, exceeding the next-best method by 4.92-8.85 percentage points.Conclusion: A single Pancreas-MedNeXt model segments tumors, pancreatic subregions, and OARs on diagnostic and MR-Linac MRI, which could streamline contouring for pancreatic cancer radiotherapy.

title: bf16 Rounding Silently Discards Most RL Policy Updates: A Hidden Training-Inference Mismatch and an Unbiased One-Line Fix
authors: Andrew Gao, William Gao
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training of language models keeps fp32 master weights in the optimizer and serves rollouts from a bf16 copy produced by round-to-nearest conversion. At the learning rates in common use, most per-step updates are smaller than half a bf16 spacing and the conversion discards them: on Qwen3-1.7B only 0.4-0.5% of served weights change per step, and the policy that generates the training data lags the optimizer by 50-150 steps. Existing mismatch corrections cannot see this lag because they compare two copies downstream of the same rounding. We propose Fair Cast: export the master with an unbiased rounding rule (stochastic rounding or error feedback) and compute the training loss on the served copy. The change is one line at the export call, adds no hyperparameters and costs 22-38 ms per export of 1.7B parameters. Across 25 matched seed-pairs on Qwen3-0.6B to 4B with AdamW and Muon, Fair Cast is ahead on 18, tied on 6 and behind on 1, with a mean gain of 6.1 points; on zebra puzzles it reaches 0.57 +/- 0.16 over four runs where round-to-nearest collapses to 0.33 +/- 0.10. It also makes the saved fp32 checkpoint agree with the served model, and it exposes the implicit lag of round-to-nearest as a regularizer that can be restored explicitly when a task needs it.

title: BABA-Bench: Evaluating Long-Horizon Patient-Advocacy Agents
authors: Shriram Vasudevan, Videet Mehta, Connor Sweeney
abstract: An LLM agent that helps a patient get care must do two things. It must reach the correct outcome, and it must follow the necessary procedure. For example, the agent must get the patient's permission before it shares the patient's records. We introduce BABA-Bench, a benchmark of 47 interactive worlds. We built each world from a de-identified, real patient advocacy case that expert advocates reviewed. In each world, the agent must find hidden information and coordinate insurers, clinics, suppliers, pharmacies, and community organizations. The engine checks each action at the time the agent does it. It checks if the agent has permission, if the agent has evidence for the action, and if the action is prohibited. We evaluated 14 frontier models with three runs on each world, for a total of 1,974 runs. Agents often reached the correct outcome by an invalid route. Of the 921 runs that reached all required outcomes, 254 (28%) did not follow the necessary procedure. Claude Opus 5 reached all required outcomes in 81.6% of its runs, but only 52.5% of its runs passed all checks. When we gave two models a verified route, their pass rates increased from 29.8% to 91.5% and from 44.0% to 97.2%. For these models, the main problem is to find a route, not to execute it.

title: Where, When, and How Many Bits? Scaling Laws for SGD with Stochastic Rounding
authors: Zhichao Wang, Michael W. Mahoney
abstract: Low-precision training reduces computation but introduces additional rounding error. We theoretically study how stochastic rounding (SR) affects prediction risk as model size, training time, and precision change. We consider a two-layer linear network with a fixed random first layer, trained by mini-batch SGD on fresh Gaussian data with power-law spectra. At each SGD step, the features used in forward and backward computations are rounded independently. We prove matched upper and lower bounds on prediction error for the final model and for uniform parameter averaging, with general learning-rate and precision schedules chosen before training. For fixed precisions and constant learning rates with parameter averaging, we derive how the smallest prediction error decreases with compute, and we identify model sizes and training times that achieve this optimal-compute scaling. Rounding only the forward features preserves the compute scaling of exact arithmetic, while rounding backward features changes it. Averaging parameters can change which computation needs higher precision and when higher precision is useful. Our results also give bit requirements for a given accuracy tolerance and show how backward rounding can change learning-rate schedule design. At a fixed compute budget, lower precision can improve prediction when the benefit of a larger model or longer training outweighs the additional SR-induced error. Model simulations illustrate these tradeoffs, and experiments with an MLP and a small transformer examine rounding choices beyond the theoretical model.

title: Grounding Image Composition with Label-Conditioned Visual Evidence
authors: Armin Dadras, Tingyu Lin, Robert Sablatnig, Franziska Proksa, Markus Seidl
abstract: Image composition labels such as center, diagonal, or rule of thirds describe visual structure rather than object categories. KU-PCP provides image-level labels and class-specific geometric elements, but does not show which visible regions people associate with each of its nine classes. We introduce KU-PCP Elements (KU-PCPE), a label-conditioned region-evidence benchmark for photographic composition. Given an image and a label already judged applicable, the task is to segment the visible regions that explain why the label applies. KU-PCPE contains 4,093 single-annotator training masks and a 1,327-task expert test split with three masks per image-label task. The annotations also include exploratory segment-versus-line ratings that describe whether region or semantic-guideline evidence better explains the label. A held-out expert reaches .867 Dice against the other experts, while the strongest deployable model reaches .664, a proposal oracle .672, and the best vision-language model (VLM) proposal selector .395. KU-PCPE exposes the gap between recognizing a composition label and grounding the human-aligned visual evidence that makes it plausible in a particular image.
zh_title: 基于标签条件视觉证据的图像构图基础
translation: 图像构图标签，例如“中心构图”、“对角线构图”或“三分法则”，描述的是视觉结构而非物体类别。KU-PCP提供了图像级标签和特定类别的几何元素，但没有显示人们将哪些可见区域与它的九个类别中的每一个关联起来。我们引入了KU-PCP元素（KU-PCPE），这是一个用于摄影构图的标签条件区域证据基准。给定一幅图像和一个已被判断适用的标签，任务是分割解释该标签适用的可见区域。KU-PCPE包含4,093个单标注者训练掩码和一个包含1,327个任务的专家测试集，每个图像-标签任务有三个掩码。标注还包括探索性的“区域与线条”评分，用于描述是区域证据还是语义指导证据更好地解释了标签。一个被保留的专家在与其他专家的对比中达到了0.867的Dice系数，而最强的可部署模型达到了0.664，一个提案预言机达到了0.672，最佳的视觉-语言模型（VLM）提案选择器达到了0.395。KU-PCPE揭示了识别构图标签与将使之在特定图像中合理的人类对齐视觉证据进行“落地”之间的差距。
tldr: 本文引入了KU-PCP Elements (KU-PCPE)，这是一个用于摄影构图的标签条件区域证据基准。其主要任务是分割出解释构图标签为何适用于图像的可见区域，并揭示了识别构图标签与定位人类对齐视觉证据之间的差距。
ai_comments: 这篇论文通过引入KU-PCPE数据集，创新性地解决了图像构图理解中“标签与视觉证据关联”的关键问题，填补了现有研究的空白。它不仅提供了一个新的、严格的基准来评估模型对构图标签深层语义的理解能力，而且通过量化不同模型与人类专家之间的差距，明确指出了当前机器视觉在理解艺术和美学元素方面的局限性。特别是其对“区域与线条”证据的探索，为理解人类如何感知和解释构图提供了新的视角。该工作对于推动机器对图像美学和构图原则的理解具有重要意义。
motivation: 现有的KU-PCP数据集提供了图像级标签和特定类别的几何元素，但未能明确指出人们将哪些可见区域与每种构图类别相关联，这导致难以理解构图标签背后的具体视觉基础。
method: 本文引入了KU-PCP Elements (KU-PCPE) 数据集，这是一个标签条件区域证据基准，用于解决图像构图的视觉证据落地问题。任务是给定一幅图像和已判断适用的构图标签，模型需要分割出解释该标签适用的可见区域。KU-PCPE包含4,093个单标注者训练掩码，以及一个包含1,327个任务的专家测试集，其中每个图像-标签任务有三个掩码。标注还包括探索性的“区域与线条”评分，以描述区域证据或语义指导证据是否更好地解释了标签。
results: 在KU-PCPE基准上，一个被保留的专家与其他专家之间的Dice系数达到0.867。最强的可部署模型达到了0.664，一个提案预言机达到了0.672，而最佳的视觉-语言模型（VLM）提案选择器仅达到0.395。这些结果揭示了识别构图标签与定位使其在特定图像中合理的人类对齐视觉证据之间存在显著差距。
conclusion: KU-PCPE基准揭示了在识别图像构图标签与将这些标签与人类对齐的视觉证据进行关联（即“落地”）之间存在显著差距。

title: Optimization Techniques for Solving the Minimum Red--Blue Separating Set Problem with an Application to Human--AI Text Separation
authors: Marko Djukanović, Staša Vujičić Stanković, Žiga Zebec, Christian Blum
abstract: We study the so-called Minimum Red''Blue Separating Set Problem (MRBSSP) which arises from computational geometry. In particular, we propose a compact Set-Cover ILP formulation, safe preprocessing rules, a Greedy Randomized Adaptive Search Procedure (GRASP), and two exact approaches: one is based on Logic-Based Benders Decomposition (LBBD) approach, and the second represents a novel Branch-and-Benders-Cut (BBC) approach. These two exact approaches are compared to ILP--alongside GRASP and the Variable Neighborhood Search (VNS) from literature. Experiments on 250 random graphs with up to 500 vertices reveal complementary strengths: ILP yields the best feasible solutions, LBBD provides the strongest lower bounds and smallest mean optimality gap, and BBC certifies optimality most frequently. We further introduce an NLP application distinguishing human- and AI-generated texts through vocabulary-based graph features. On 42 instances, BBC achieves the smallest mean optimality gap, certifying 16 optima, while GRASP outperforms VNS. Structural analysis of optimal vocabulary separators identifies 113 mandatory and 151 replaceable features across 272 tests, highlighting substantial variability among optimal solutions. Overall, our results demonstrate the effectiveness of complementary optimization strategies and the interpretability of optimal vocabulary-based discrimination.
zh_title: 优化解决最小红蓝分离集问题的技术及其在人机文本分离中的应用
translation: 我们研究了计算几何中出现的所谓最小红蓝分离集问题（MRBSSP）。具体来说，我们提出了一个紧凑的集合覆盖整数线性规划（ILP）公式、安全预处理规则、一种贪婪随机自适应搜索过程（GRASP），以及两种精确方法：一种是基于逻辑Benders分解（LBBD）方法，第二种代表了一种新颖的分支Benders割（BBC）方法。这两种精确方法与ILP以及文献中的GRASP和变邻域搜索（VNS）进行了比较。在多达500个顶点的250个随机图上的实验揭示了互补的优势：ILP产生最佳可行解，LBBD提供最强的下界和最小的平均最优性差距，而BBC最频繁地证明最优性。我们进一步引入了一个NLP应用，通过基于词汇的图特征来区分人类和AI生成的文本。在42个实例上，BBC实现了最小的平均最优性差距，证明了16个最优解，而GRASP优于VNS。对最优词汇分离器的结构分析确定了272项测试中的113个强制特征和151个可替换特征，突出了最优解之间的显著变异性。总的来说，我们的结果证明了互补优化策略的有效性以及基于最优词汇判别的可解释性。
tldr: 本文研究并提出了多种优化技术（ILP, GRASP, LBBD, BBC）来解决最小红蓝分离集问题，并将其应用于区分人类和AI生成的文本，实验结果展示了这些方法的互补性和有效性。
ai_comments: 该研究通过提出多种互补的优化技术（包括启发式和精确方法）来解决最小红蓝分离集问题，展示了其在理论和实践中的重要性。特别值得注意的是，其将MRBSSP应用于区分人机生成文本这一前沿且具有挑战性的NLP任务，通过构建基于词汇的图特征，为文本归属识别提供了一种新颖且可解释的优化方法。不同方法在性能上的互补性也为实际应用提供了灵活的选择。
motivation: 研究计算几何中出现的最小红蓝分离集问题（MRBSSP），并将其应用于通过基于词汇的图特征区分人类和AI生成的文本。
method: 提出了紧凑的集合覆盖整数线性规划（ILP）公式、安全预处理规则、贪婪随机自适应搜索过程（GRASP），以及两种精确方法：基于逻辑Benders分解（LBBD）方法和新的分支Benders割（BBC）方法。这些方法与文献中的ILP、GRASP和变邻域搜索（VNS）进行了比较。
results: 在包含多达500个顶点的250个随机图上的实验表明：ILP产生最佳可行解，LBBD提供最强下界和最小平均最优性差距，BBC最频繁地证明最优性。在42个NLP实例上，BBC实现了最小平均最优性差距，证明了16个最优解，而GRASP优于VNS。对最优词汇分离器的结构分析确定了272项测试中的113个强制特征和151个可替换特征，突出了最优解之间的显著变异性。
conclusion: 研究结果证明了互补优化策略的有效性以及基于最优词汇的判别方法的解释性。

title: Evaluating Structural and SAT Attack Resilience in Cryptographic Dynamic Logic Locking via Keystream Capping
authors: Nahush Tambe, Naseeruddin Lodge, Vineet Chadalavada, Fareena Saqib
abstract: Untrusted third-party entities throughout the semiconductor supply chain expose proprietary hardware intellectual property to reverse engineering, piracy, and overproduction. While logic locking counters this threat by embedding key-dependent logic, conventional static key-gates remain vulnerable to both oracle-guided SAT attacks and structural removal attacks due to their time-invariant netlist signatures. Dynamic schemes such as STREAMLOCK mitigate oracle attacks by continuously masking signals with cryptographic keystream, achieving near 50\% Hamming distance output corruption under incorrect keys with low hardware overhead. However, confining key-gates to primary outputs leaves internal combinational cones vulnerable to single-tap structural bypasses. This work extends dynamic logic locking by distributing key-gates within internal paths prioritized via fault-propagation analysis. The original and internally-hardened architectures are evaluated against structural removal attacks and a bounded, unrolling-based SAT-style attack across three ISCAS'85 benchmarks. Distributing masking internally raises the uninformed attacker's brute-force search space from 6 candidate node subsets to over $10^{45}$ for the largest benchmark. Crucially, empirical analysis reveals that topological relocation alone does not prevent algebraic key extraction when wide circuits expose numerous keystream bits per clock cycle. To eliminate this leak, a keystream-bit reuse cap is introduced to restrict per-cycle exposure independent of circuit width. Under this constraint, SAT-solver tractability encounters an immediate computational cliff, transitioning sharply from rapid under-constrained solving to timeout thresholds without disclosing the secret key. Integrating fault-aware internal placement with keystream reuse capping delivers joint resilience against structural bypasses and bounded SAT attacks.
zh_title: 通过密钥流上限评估密码学动态逻辑锁定中的结构与SAT攻击抗性
translation: 半导体供应链中的不可信第三方实体使专有硬件知识产权（IP）面临逆向工程、盗版和过度生产的威胁。虽然逻辑锁定技术通过嵌入密钥依赖逻辑来应对这一威胁，但传统的静态密钥门因其时不变的网表特征，仍易受到基于预言机指导的SAT攻击和结构移除攻击。诸如STREAMLOCK等动态方案通过使用密码学密钥流持续掩码信号来缓解预言机攻击，在低硬件开销下使错误密钥产生接近50%汉明距离的输出破坏。然而，仅将密钥门限制在主输出端会使内部组合逻辑锥面临单抽头结构旁路的威胁。本研究通过故障传播分析对内部路径进行优先级排序并分布式部署密钥门，对动态逻辑锁定进行了扩展。在三个ISCAS'85基准测试上，对原始架构与内部加固架构针对结构移除攻击以及基于有界展开的SAT式攻击进行了评估。在内部署掩码使无先验知识攻击者的暴力搜索空间在最大基准电路上从6个候选节点子集大幅提升至超过10^45。更重要的是，实证分析表明，当宽电路在每个时钟周期暴露过多密钥流比特时，仅靠拓扑重定位无法阻止代数密钥提取。为消除此类泄露，本文引入了密钥流比特重用上限，独立于电路位宽限制每周期的暴露量。在此约束下，SAT求解器的易解性遭遇了断崖式的计算瓶颈，从快速的欠约束求解急剧转变为超时状态且不泄露密钥。将故障感知的内部放置与密钥流重用上限相结合，实现了抵御结构旁路和有界SAT攻击的双重弹性。
tldr: 本文结合故障感知内部密钥门放置与密钥流重用上限技术，有效解决了动态逻辑锁定的结构旁路和SAT代数提取漏洞。
ai_comments: 本研究的创新点在于揭示了动态逻辑锁定中仅靠拓扑重定位无法防御代数密钥提取的缺陷，并提出了“密钥流重用上限（keystream-bit reuse cap）”这一轻量且有效的约束机制；其重要性体现在实现了结构旁路防御与抗SAT攻击的兼顾；局限性在于测试仅在三个ISCAS'85基准电路上进行，且防御的是有界展开SAT攻击，对更大规模现代电路和高级攻击形式的泛化能力仍有待进一步验证。
motivation: 传统静态逻辑锁定易受SAT和结构移除攻击；现有的动态逻辑锁定方案（如STREAMLOCK）虽然能利用密码学密钥流动态掩码抵御预言机攻击，但若仅将密钥门限制在主输出端，内部逻辑仍易受单抽头结构旁路攻击；此外，位宽较大的电路每个周期会暴露过多密钥流比特，导致代数密钥提取仍然可行。
method: 1. 利用故障传播分析（fault-propagation analysis）优先在内部路径中分布放置密钥门，以加固内部组合逻辑锥；2. 引入密钥流比特重用上限（keystream-bit reuse cap），限制每个时钟周期暴露的密钥流比特数，使其与电路位宽解耦；3. 在三个ISCAS'85基准电路上，针对结构移除攻击和基于有界展开的SAT式攻击进行安全评估。
results: 1. 内部分布式掩码将最大基准测试中攻击者的穷举搜索空间从6个候选节点子集激增至超过10^45；2. 仅进行拓扑重定位无法防止宽电路中的代数密钥提取；3. 引入密钥流重用上限后，SAT求解器遭遇显著的计算断崖，求解过程直接从欠约束快速求解骤变至超时阈值，且未泄露密钥。
conclusion: 将基于故障感知的内部密钥门放置与密钥流重用上限机制相结合，能够同时实现对结构旁路攻击和有界展开SAT攻击的有效防御。

title: EDU-Jev Training System-One Decision Models for Education
authors: Jiazheng Li, Yulan He
abstract: Many automated decisions in education involve choosing from a fixed set of options: assigning a rubric score, checking whether an answer meets a marking criterion, or identifying the first wrong step in a solution. Generative language models are increasingly used to make these decisions, but their responses require parsing, longer outputs increase inference costs, and confidence expressed in words does not necessarily reflect the probability of being correct. We present EDU-Jev, a family of single-pass ("System One") decision models at 0.8B, 2B and 4B parameters. Given an assessment context and a question with predefined answer options, the model returns a probability distribution over those options without generating text. A pointer head scores a marker for each option, ensuring the predictions are restricted to the allowed choices. Training uses a single supervised stage with soft cross-entropy against the available target label distributions; calibration is assessed empirically. Across twelve education benchmarks, EDU-Jev 4B achieves an average accuracy of 67.6%, exceeding the strongest of five commercial decision APIs by 9.4 percentage points and the best open 4B decision model by 18.7 points. On four cross-domain education sets, it matches the strongest API, which remains ahead on general decision-making and reasoning tasks. The 2B model processes about 150 decisions per second on a single H100 GPU.
comment: 16 pages, 3 figures, 4 tables. Work in progress
zh_title: EDU-Jev：训练面向教育的“系统一”决策模型
translation: 教育领域的许多自动化决策涉及从固定选项中进行选择：如分配评分准则得分、检查答案是否符合批改标准，或识别解题过程中的第一个错误步骤。生成式语言模型越来越多地被用于做出这些决策，但其输出需要解析，较长的输出会增加推理成本，而且用文字表达的置信度并不一定反映正确的概率。我们提出了 EDU-Jev，这是一个具有 0.8B、2B 和 4B 参数规模的单次前向（“系统一”）决策模型家族。在给定评估上下文和包含预定义答案选项的问题时，该模型返回这些选项的概率分布，而无需生成文本。指针头为每个选项标记评分，确保预测严格限制在允许的选项范围内。训练采用单一监督阶段，针对可用的目标标签分布使用软交叉熵进行优化；校准效果则通过实证进行评估。在 12 个教育基准测试中，EDU-Jev 4B 实现了 67.6% 的平均准确率，比 5 个商业决策 API 中最强的一款高出 9.4 个百分点，比最强的开源 4B 决策模型高出 18.7 个百分点。在 4 个跨领域教育数据集上，其表现追平了最强的商业 API（该 API 在通用决策和推理任务上仍保持领先）。2B 模型在单块 H100 GPU 上每秒可处理约 150 次决策。
tldr: 针对教育固定选项决策任务，提出了无需文本生成的单次前向EDU-Jev模型，准确率超越商业API且推理速度极快。
ai_comments: 该研究针对教育领域中大量属于固定选项判别的决策任务，摒弃了昂贵且容易产生解析偏差的自回归生成方式，创新性地采用“系统一”（单次前向传播）直接输出概率分布的架构，大幅提升了推理吞吐量（2B模型达150次决策/秒）并改善了校准度。其局限在于通用决策与复杂推理能力仍落后于顶尖商业API，且主要适用于预定义选项的封闭式判断场景。
motivation: 教育领域的许多自动化决策（如评分准则、答案批改标准核对、解题步骤错因定位）本质上属于从固定选项集合中做选择。传统的生成式语言模型需要对输出文本进行解析、长文本输出导致推理成本高昂，且用文字表达的置信度往往无法真实反映判断的正确概率。
method: 提出了EDU-Jev模型家族（0.8B、2B、4B参数规模），采用单次前向传递（系统一）直接输出预定义选项的概率分布而无需生成文本。架构上利用指针头（pointer head）为每个选项标记评分以约束预测范围；训练上采用单阶段监督学习，使用软交叉熵（soft cross-entropy）拟合目标标签分布，并对置信度校准进行实证评估。
results: 在12个教育基准上，EDU-Jev 4B达到67.6%的平均准确率，比测试的5个商业决策API中表现最好的高出9.4个百分点，比开源最强4B决策模型高出18.7个百分点；在4个跨领域教育数据集上追平最强商业API（商业API在通用决策和推理任务上仍保持领先）；EDU-Jev 2B模型在单块H100 GPU上每秒可处理约150次决策。
conclusion: EDU-Jev证明了轻量级、无文本生成的单次前向决策模型在教育垂直任务中不仅能够大幅降低计算与解析开销，还能在准确率上超越更大型的通用商业决策API，为低延迟、高可靠的教育自动化评估提供了极具实用价值的解决方案。

title: Payroll Fraud Detection in Synthetic HR/ERP Graphs: An Inductive Comparison of Rules, Path Features, and Graph Neural Networks
authors: Xiaobo Chen, Genliang Zhu, Ziyuan Wang, Chu Wang
abstract: Payroll-fraud screening requires finding hidden employee--payee links while distinguishing suspicious relationships from legitimate ones. We formulate this problem as inductive link prediction and entity ranking on synthetic human-resources and enterprise resource planning (HR/ERP) graphs, with unseen organizations and a matched benign twin for every planted case. An original study on 24 held-out organizations and a prospectively frozen extension compare analyst rules, explicit path features and graph neural networks (GNNs). A tuned gradient-boosted model on chained-join features achieved the highest overall link average precision (AP; 0.823), above the GraIL-style GNN (0.663); its 4-hop AP was 0.646 versus 0.272. Thus, the observed multi-hop gain is not specific to GNNs. On a new synthetic cohort with 2.0% positive entities, chained-join boosting again led (AP 0.798); the relational entity GNN also exceeded record-aware rules (0.707 versus 0.504). At a 2% review budget, their precision was 0.695 versus 0.602. Under 40% failed identifier joins, the entity GNN ranked above chained-join boosting (AP 0.712 versus 0.683, descriptively). Structure-only auditing exposed a shortcut in the initial generator; matched twins reduced the audited twin-pool AUROC to 0.493--0.514. These results separate multi-hop candidate discovery, record-based discrimination and review prioritization within an explicit synthetic evaluation design. Code and data are available from the authors on request.
zh_title: 合成HR/ERP图中的薪资欺诈检测：规则、路径特征与图神经网络的归纳式对比研究
translation: 薪资欺诈筛查需要发现隐藏的员工—收款人链接，同时将可疑关系与合法关系区分开来。我们将该问题形式化为合成人力资源与企业资源计划（HR/ERP）图上的归纳式链接预测和实体排序，测试集包含未见过的组织，且为每个植入欺诈案例匹配了良性孪生对照。通过对24个保留组织的原生研究以及前瞻性冻结扩展，我们对比了分析师规则、显式路径特征和图神经网络（GNN）。基于链式连接特征微调的梯度提升模型取得了最高的整体链接平均精度（AP；0.823），高于GraIL类GNN（0.663）；其4跳AP为0.646，相比之下GNN为0.272。因此，观察到的多跳增益并非GNN所独有。在一个正例实体占比2.0%的新合成队列中，链式连接提升模型再次领先（AP 0.798）；关系实体GNN也优于感知记录的规则（0.707对比0.504）。在2%的审核预算下，两者的精确率分别为0.695和0.602。在40%标识符连接失败的情况下，实体GNN排序优于链式连接提升模型（描述性分析中AP为0.712对比0.683）。仅基于结构的审计揭示了初始生成器中的捷径；配对孪生使审计孪生池的AUROC降至0.493–0.514。这些结果在显式的合成评估设计中，将多跳候选发现、基于记录的辨别与审核优先级排序有效区分开来。代码和数据可按要求向作者索取。
tldr: 对比规则、显式路径特征与GNN在企业图薪资欺诈检测中的表现，发现显式路径特征模型整体表现最优，但GNN在连接缺失时鲁棒性更强。
ai_comments: 该研究创新性地使用合成HR/ERP图并引入配对良性孪生（matched twins）消除了图生成器中的结构捷径，严谨地对比了传统路径特征（如梯度提升树链式连接）与GNN在归纳链接预测和实体排序中的表现，揭示了多跳推理收益并非GNN独有，对实际企业欺诈检测系统的模型选型具有重要参考价值。
motivation: 薪资欺诈筛查需要发现隐藏的“员工-收款人”关联，同时区分可疑关系与合法关系；需要在未见过的组织图结构中进行归纳推理。
method: 将问题建模为合成HR/ERP图上的归纳式链接预测与实体排序任务，并引入配对良性孪生案例；对比了分析师规则、显式路径特征（基于链式连接特征的微调梯度提升模型）以及图神经网络（GraIL类GNN、关系实体GNN）。
results: 链式连接梯度提升模型在整体链接AP（0.823 vs GNN 0.663）及4跳AP（0.646 vs 0.272）上均大幅领先；在2.0%正样本的新队列中，其AP达到0.798，而关系实体GNN（0.707）优于规则（0.504）；在40%标识符连接失效时，实体GNN更具鲁棒性（AP 0.712 vs 0.683）；结构审计和良性孪生消除了生成器捷径。
conclusion: 多跳收益并非GNN所独有，梯度提升树结合链式连接特征在多数指标上优于GNN，但在标识符连接大量失败时实体GNN表现更优；该基准设计成功解耦了多跳候选发现、基于记录的辨别和审核优先级排序。

title: CIRCE Divines LLM Task Complexity from Constraint Structure
authors: Chenhao Hong, Jiakai Xu, Kaushiki Singh, Yusen Zhang, Eugene Wu
abstract:
Estimating whether a problem is too complex for a large language model (LLM) before the model attempts it can guide model routing, how to allocate test-time compute, and suggest the need for new tools to aid the agent. While existing estimators rely on the problem text, LLM-annotated task difficulty labels, or signals obtained after a model attempts to solve the problem, such as its hidden states, none explicitly leverage the constraint structure inherent in the problem: the variables to assign and how the constraints over them interact.
  We introduce CIRCE, which extracts a problem's structure by using a cheap LLM to construct a Constraint Intermediate Representation that deterministically compiles into the constraint graph. Across seven reasoning benchmarks (including SAT, logic, and math) and four LLMs, even a randomly initialized GNN encoder improves predictions of LLM response correctness, reducing negative log-likelihood from 0.465 to 0.423 and increasing AUROC from 0.691 to 0.727 relative to the strongest baseline for each metric.
zh_title: CIRCE：从约束结构中预测大语言模型的任务复杂度
translation: 在大语言模型（LLM）尝试解决问题之前，预估该问题对其而言是否过于复杂，可以指导模型路由、合理分配测试时计算资源，并提示是否需要新工具来辅助智能体。现有的预估方法往往依赖于问题文本、LLM 标注的任务难度标签，或者模型尝试求解后获取的信号（如其隐藏状态），但都没有显式地利用问题中固有的约束结构——即待赋值的变量以及变量间约束是如何相互作用的。我们提出了 CIRCE，它通过使用廉价的 LLM 构建一个约束中间表示（Constraint Intermediate Representation），该表示可以确定性地编译为约束图，从而提取出问题的结构。在涵盖 SAT、逻辑和数学等 7 个推理基准以及 4 个 LLM 的实验中，即使是随机初始化的 GNN 编码器也能改善对 LLM 回答正确性的预测，相较于各指标的最强基准，负对数似然从 0.465 降低至 0.423，AUROC 从 0.691 提升至 0.727。
tldr: CIRCE 通过将复杂推理问题转化为约束图并结合 GNN，在模型解答前即可高精度预测 LLM 的任务复杂度与正确率。
ai_comments: 该论文的创新点在于摆脱了以往仅依赖文本表层特征或模型推理后隐状态的评估模式，抓住逻辑推理任务的核心本质——约束满足结构，通过低成本LLM将自然语言编译为显式约束图。令人瞩目的是，即便仅采用随机初始化的GNN也能取得超越强基线的性能，充分证明了约束拓扑结构本身包含强大的任务复杂度先验信息。潜在局限可能在于其依赖低成本LLM生成约束中间表示的质量，在形式化较弱或常识性复杂的任务上的鲁棒性仍有待观察。
motivation: 在 LLM 尝试解决问题之前提前预估任务复杂度，能够有效指导模型路由、优化测试时计算资源分配以及决策是否引入外部工具；而现有预测方法仅依赖问题文本、模型自标注难度或解题后的隐状态，未能显式利用问题中固有的变量及其约束交互结构。
method: 提出了 CIRCE 方法：利用低成本 LLM 将问题解析并构建为“约束中间表示”（Constraint Intermediate Representation, CIR），再将其确定性编译为约束图，随后采用图神经网络（GNN）编码器（实验中即使随机初始化也有效）对图结构进行编码，进而预测 LLM 求解该任务的正确性。
results: 在涵盖 SAT、逻辑和数学等 7 个推理基准以及 4 个 LLM 的评测中，即便仅使用随机初始化的 GNN 编码器，CIRCE 也能显著改善对 LLM 回答正确性的预测能力；与各指标的最强基线相比，负对数似然（NLL）从 0.465 降低至 0.423，AUROC 从 0.691 提高至 0.727。
conclusion: 显式利用问题内在的变量交互和约束结构（编译为约束图），能够显著提升在模型求解前预测LLM任务复杂度与正确率的精度。

title: Verifying Text-to-SQL Queries under Changing Business Semantics
authors: Genliang Zhu, Xiaobo Chen, Ziyuan Wang, Chu Wang
abstract: In text-to-SQL and AI-agent analytics, successful SQL execution does not establish semantic correctness under changing business definitions. We study revalidation of fixed queries after changes to refund attribution, tax treatment, eligible populations and exchange-rate dates. An executable verification profile binds the requested revision and knowledge cutoff to legal counterexample data and exact monetary comparison. A preregistered confirmation on 32 newly authored revision families and two local producer bundles retains 192 query-definition cells: 144 nonconforming, 36 finite-suite agreeing and 12 unresolved. Of the nonconforming cells, 63 agree on the current snapshot. At an eight-ledger budget, obligation-guided checking detects 137 discrepancies versus 127 for generic ordering, a paired difference of 6.9 percentage points (family bootstrap 95% interval [2.1, 13.6]; exact family sign-flip p=0.0156). Every ledger arm rejects zero of the 36 agreeing cells. Current-obligation and equal-weight scoring match the guided result, identifying coverage rather than revision-specific priority as the observed source of benefit. Controlled assays, a natural-query pilot and repeated samples provide separate mechanism and robustness evidence. A legal discrepancy refutes conformance; agreement remains restricted to the recorded suite. The study establishes an auditable business-semantic revalidation profile within its authored schema and local-model scope.
zh_title: 业务语义变更下的Text-to-SQL查询验证
translation: 在Text-to-SQL和AI智能体分析中，当业务定义发生变化时，SQL成功执行并不能证明其语义正确。我们研究了在退款归属、税务处理、合格人群和汇率日期等变更后，对固定查询的重新验证问题。一种可执行的验证配置文件将所请求的修订和知识截止时间与合法的反例数据及精确货币比较绑定在一起。在对32个新编写的修订族和两个本地生成包进行的预注册确认中，保留了192个查询-定义单元：144个不符合项、36个有限套件一致项和12个未解决项。在不符合的单元中，有63个在当前快照上表现一致。在8账本预算下，义务引导检查检测出137个差异，而通用排序检测出127个，配对差异为6.9个百分点（修订族Bootstrap 95%置信区间为[2.1, 13.6]；精确族符号翻转p=0.0156）。每个账本分支对36个一致单元的拒绝数均为0。当前义务评分和等权重评分与引导结果相匹配，表明覆盖范围而非特定于修订的优先级是观察到的收益来源。受控测试、自然查询试点和重复抽样提供了机制与鲁棒性的独立证据。合法的差异能够否定一致性；而一致性仍局限于已记录的测试套件。该研究在其构建的模式和本地模型范围内建立了一个可审计的业务语义重验证配置文件。
tldr: 本文提出了一种可执行验证方案，利用合法反例数据与义务引导检查，高效重验证业务规则变更下的Text-to-SQL查询语义正确性。
ai_comments: 该研究极具实际应用价值，敏锐地指出了当前Text-to-SQL在企业落地中的痛点——SQL虽能成功运行，但业务规则（如税率、退款口径等）发生漂移时会导致静默错误。其提出的可审计重验证框架与反例驱动检测方法兼具实用性与严谨性。局限在于目前的实验验证仍受限于特定设计的模式与测试套件范围，测试套件内的一致无法严格推论全局语义等价。
motivation: 在Text-to-SQL和AI智能体分析场景中，SQL成功执行并不意味着业务定义变更后依然保持语义正确。当退款归属、税务处理、合格人群与汇率日期等业务规则改变时，亟需对已有固定查询进行重新验证。
method: 提出了一种可执行验证配置文件（executable verification profile），将业务修订请求和知识截止时间与合法的反例数据及精确货币比较相结合；采用义务引导检查（obligation-guided checking）机制，并在32个新修订族及本地生成包构建的192个查询-定义单元上进行预注册评估。
results: 在192个查询-定义单元中（144个不符合、36个有限套件一致、12个未解决），有63个不符合单元在当前快照上表面一致。在8账本预算下，义务引导检查检测出137个差异，较通用排序的127个显著提升6.9个百分点（p=0.0156），且对36个一致单元的误拒率为0；分析证实收益来源主要为测试覆盖率而非修订特定的优先级。
conclusion: 合法的差异能够证伪查询的合规性，而验证一致性仍局限于已记录的测试套件。该研究在其构建的模式与本地模型范围内，成功建立了一套可审计的业务语义重验证机制。

title: AIFaultBench: A Reproducible Benchmark of Real-World Faults in AI Software Systems
authors: Mehil B Shah, Mohammad Masudur Rahman, Foutse Khomh
abstract: AI-based software systems remain difficult to debug because their failures can involve interactions among code, models, data, dependencies, hardware, and execution environments. Existing benchmarks cover specific classes of AI systems, while concerns about fault realism and reproducibility highlight the need for documented execution conditions and evidence. We present AIFaultBench, a benchmark of 770 real-world bugs from 105 AI-based software repositories across 76 organizations. It covers six classes of AI systems: machine learning, deep learning, reinforcement learning, systems based on large language models, agentic AI, and AI tooling and infrastructure. Each bug record connects the original report and affected codebase to structured metadata, environment setup scripts, a reproduction trigger, and investigation evidence. We reproduced 652 bugs (84.7%) under the recorded execution conditions and documented the outcomes of the remaining 118 attempts. Through its broad coverage, documented reproduction evidence, and common structure, AIFaultBench supports empirical studies of AI faults, debugging tool evaluation, practical failure investigation, and teaching with real-world examples.
comment: Under Review - ICSE 2027 Tool Demonstration and Data Showcase Track
zh_title: AIFaultBench：一个可复现的AI软件系统真实世界故障基准
translation: 基于人工智能的软件系统仍然难以调试，因为它们的故障可能涉及代码、模型、数据、依赖项、硬件和执行环境之间的相互作用。现有的基准测试涵盖了特定类别的AI系统，而对故障真实性和可复现性的担忧凸显了对记录的执行条件和证据的需求。我们提出了AIFaultBench，这是一个包含来自76个组织的105个基于AI的软件仓库中的770个真实世界bug的基准。它涵盖了六类AI系统：机器学习、深度学习、强化学习、基于大语言模型的系统、智能体AI以及AI工具和基础设施。每个bug记录都将原始报告和受影响的代码库连接到结构化元数据、环境设置脚本、复现触发器和调查证据。我们在记录的执行条件下复现了652个bug（84.7%），并记录了其余118次尝试的结果。通过其广泛的覆盖范围、记录的复现证据和共同的结构，AIFaultBench支持对AI故障的实证研究、调试工具评估、实际故障调查以及用真实世界的例子进行教学。
tldr: AIFaultBench是一个包含770个真实世界AI软件故障的全面、可复现基准，涵盖6大类AI系统，为AI调试研究和工具评估提供了重要支持。
ai_comments: 该论文填补了AI软件系统缺乏全面、真实、可复现故障基准的空白，具有很高的实用价值和学术研究意义，支持了经验研究、调试工具评估以及教学等多个场景。
motivation: 现有的AI系统基准仅涵盖特定类别，且真实故障的真实性和可复现性存在不足，缺乏记录明确的执行条件和证据，导致AI软件系统难以调试。
method: 构建了一个包含770个来自105个AI软件仓库的真实故障的基准库（AIFaultBench），涵盖6大类AI系统，并为每个故障提供结构化元数据、环境设置脚本、复现触发器和调查证据。
results: 成功在记录的执行条件下复现了652个bug（占84.7%），并记录了其余118次尝试的结果。
conclusion: AIFaultBench是一个全面、可复现的真实AI软件系统故障基准，通过提供结构化元数据和复现脚本，有效促进了AI故障的研究、调试工具评估和实际故障调查。

title: Robust edge multiscale space based hybrid Schwarz preconditioner for high-frequency Helmholtz problems
authors: Shubin Fu, Shihua Gong, Guanglian Li, Yulei Liao
abstract: We develop a novel hybrid Schwarz method, termed the robust edge multiscale space based hybrid Schwarz method (REMs-HS), for the efficient solution of high-frequency Helmholtz problems. The method combines a one-level restricted additive Schwarz preconditioner with impedance transmission conditions (RAS-imp) and an edge multiscale (EMs) coarse solver in a multiplicative way. A key ingredient of our construction is a modified impedance boundary condition (mIBC), which is imposed both on the subdomain problems and on the local problems that generate the EMs coarse space. Compared with the original impedance boundary condition, the mIBC makes the proposed method both stable and inexpensive theoretically. We prove that the resulting REMs-HS preconditioner gives rise to a uniform convergent fixed-point iteration for large wavenumbers. Moreover, the required resolution conditions are substantially relaxed. Only a mild condition on the level parameter $\ell$ of the hierarchical coarse basis $\ell>\frac{1}{2}\log_2 k$ is needed, which is markedly weaker than the conditions in previous analyses. Extensive numerical experiments demonstrate the robustness of the proposed method for Helmholtz problems with large wavenumbers.
zh_title: 基于稳健边多尺度空间的高频Helmholtz问题混合Schwarz预条件子
translation: 我们开发了一种新型混合Schwarz方法，称为基于稳健边多尺度空间的混合Schwarz方法（REMs-HS），用于高效求解高频Helmholtz问题。该方法将具有阻抗传输条件的单层限制性加性Schwarz预条件子（RAS-imp）与边多尺度（EMs）粗求解器以乘性方式结合。我们构建的关键要素是一种修正阻抗边界条件（mIBC），它同时施加于子域问题以及生成EMs粗空间的局部问题上。与原始阻抗边界条件相比，mIBC在理论上使所提出的方法既稳定又低计算成本。我们证明了所得REMs-HS预条件子对于大波数能够产生一致收敛的不动点迭代。此外，所需的网格分辨率条件显著放宽。分层粗基底的层级参数 $\ell$ 仅需满足温和条件 $\ell>\frac{1}{2}\log_2 k$，这明显弱于以往分析中的条件。大量的数值实验展示了所提方法在求解大波数Helmholtz问题时的稳健性。
tldr: 提出了一种融合修正阻抗边界条件与边多尺度粗求解器的新型混合Schwarz预条件子，成功实现了大波数Helmholtz问题的一致收敛且显著降低了分辨率要求。
ai_comments: 该研究的创新之处在于引入了修正阻抗边界条件（mIBC），并将其有机融入边多尺度粗空间的构建与子域问题中，从而在乘性混合Schwarz框架下实现了大波数下的一致收敛性。理论上将分辨率条件大幅放宽至仅需 $\ell > \frac{1}{2}\log_2 k$，是一项显著的理论突破；局限在于摘要未详细展示三维复杂非均匀介质中的扩展性及具体并行计算规模。
motivation: 针对高频Helmholtz问题求解困难的挑战，旨在克服传统阻抗边界条件在稳定性和计算成本方面的限制，并显著放宽粗网格离散解析度的苛刻要求。
method: 提出了基于稳健边多尺度空间的混合Schwarz方法（REMs-HS）。该方法采用乘性方式结合带有阻抗传输条件的单层限制性加性Schwarz预条件子（RAS-imp）与边多尺度（EMs）粗求解器，并在子域问题及生成EMs粗空间的局部问题中均施加了修正阻抗边界条件（mIBC）。
results: 证明了REMs-HS预条件子在大波数下可诱导出一致收敛的不动点迭代；粗基底层级参数只需满足较弱的温和条件 $\ell > \frac{1}{2}\log_2 k$；数值实验验证了该方法在大波数下具有极高的稳健性。
conclusion: REMs-HS方法在理论上稳定且计算成本低，大幅放宽了解析度约束条件，能够在大波数Helmholtz问题中实现一致收敛，是一种高效且稳健的预条件子技术。

title: Flash Word : ESL Listening Support with Subtitle Skimming
authors: Yuzu Saijo, Jun Rekimoto
abstract: Listening to English audio with English subtitles is thought to be effective for ESL students to improve listening comprehension skills. However, for those who learn English as a second language it can be hard to finish English subtitles. Also they are unlikely to focus on listening while being busy reading subtitles. We propose Flash Word, a subtitling system which generates and presents shortened intralingual subtitles for English audio by detecting keywords from the script. Flash Word extracts keywords from scripts using an existing algorithm, and shows them one at a time like a flashcard. The system calculates when the keywords are being pronounced and aligns them correctly. Flash Word aims to enable ESL students to focus better on listening by minimising the cost of reading subtitles.
zh_title: Flash Word：通过字幕速览辅助ESL英语听力
translation: 听英语音频配合英文字幕被认为对ESL学生提高听力理解技能很有效。然而，对于那些将英语作为第二语言的学习者来说，可能很难读完英文字幕。此外，他们在忙于阅读字幕时也不太可能专注于听力。我们提出了 Flash Word，这是一种字幕系统，它通过从脚本中检测关键词，为英语音频生成并展示精简的语内字幕。Flash Word 利用现有算法从脚本中提取关键词，并像闪卡一样一次只显示一个关键词。该系统能够计算关键词何时被发音并进行正确定齐。Flash Word 旨在通过最小化阅读字幕的成本，使ESL学生能够更好地专注于听力。
tldr: Flash Word 通过提取关键词并以闪卡形式与音频发音精准对齐，简化英文字幕，从而帮助ESL学生专注于听力训练。
ai_comments: 该研究创新性地将闪卡机制引入视频/音频字幕呈现中，通过关键词速览替代完整句子字幕，切中了ESL学习者在阅读字幕与听力注意力分配之间的痛点；但摘要中未报告用户研究或量化评估结果，其实际教学效果和学习者接受度仍有待验证。
motivation: 听英语音频配英文字幕虽有助于ESL学习者提升听力，但学习者往往阅读速度跟不上，且忙于阅读完整字幕容易分散注意力，无法专心进行听力训练。
method: 提出 Flash Word 字幕系统：利用现有算法从音频脚本中提取关键词，计算关键词的发音时间点并实现精准时间对齐，最终以类似闪卡的形式一次仅展示一个关键词。
conclusion: Flash Word 旨在通过最大程度地减少阅读字幕带来的视觉与认知负担，使ESL学习者能够更加专注于英语听力本身。

title: RepGen: Reproducing Deep Learning Bugs through Context-Aware Code Generation and Verification
authors: Mehil B Shah, Mohammad Masudur Rahman, Foutse Khomh
abstract: Reproducing deep learning (DL) bugs is challenging because failures can involve source code, models, data, dependencies, and execution environments. Incomplete bug reports further complicate reproduction by omitting essential details. We present RepGen, an open-source tool for reproducing DL bugs through context-aware code generation and iterative verification. Given a bug report and repository, RepGen explores the codebase to build a learning-enhanced context, develop a reproduction plan, and generate candidate scripts. It refines candidates using static checks and LLM feedback to improve their correctness and relevance. When enabled, the tool prepares the execution environment, runs the script, and assesses its output against the reported failure. RepGen provides an interactive command-line interface supporting local and hosted LLMs, configurable execution budgets, and inspectable artifacts, along with a GitHub Action for automated issue processing. The underlying approach reproduced 85 of 106 real-world DL bugs (80.19%). A controlled study with 27 developers showed a 23.35% improvement in reproduction success and a 56.8% reduction in reproduction time.
comment: Under Review - ICSE 2027 Tool Demonstration and Data Showcase Track
zh_title: RepGen：通过上下文感知代码生成和验证复现深度学习错误
translation: 复现深度学习（DL）错误具有挑战性，因为故障可能涉及源代码、模型、数据、依赖项和执行环境。不完整的错误报告由于遗漏了基本细节，进一步使复现复杂化。我们提出了RepGen，一个开源工具，通过上下文感知代码生成和迭代验证来复现DL错误。给定一个错误报告和代码仓库，RepGen会探索代码库以构建学习增强的上下文，制定复现计划，并生成候选脚本。它使用静态检查和LLM反馈来优化候选脚本的正确性和相关性。启用后，该工具会准备执行环境，运行脚本，并根据报告的故障评估其输出。RepGen提供了一个支持本地和托管LLM、可配置执行预算和可检查工件的交互式命令行界面，以及一个用于自动化问题处理的GitHub Action。其底层方法复现了106个真实世界DL错误中的85个（80.19%）。一项针对27名开发人员的对照研究显示，复现成功率提高了23.35%，复现时间减少了56.8%。
tldr: RepGen是一个开源工具，它通过上下文感知代码生成和迭代验证来复现深度学习错误。它能探索代码库，生成候选脚本，并通过静态检查和LLM反馈进行优化。该工具成功复现了80.19%的真实世界深度学习错误，并显著提高了开发人员的复现成功率和效率。
ai_comments: 该论文提出了一种创新的方法，利用上下文感知代码生成和LLM反馈来自动化深度学习错误的复现过程。其重要性在于解决了DL开发中一个关键且耗时的问题，即错误复现的复杂性。通过提供一个开源工具和GitHub Action，RepGen有望显著提高DL社区的调试效率。结合LLM进行代码生成和优化是其主要的创新点。
motivation: 复现深度学习（DL）错误具有挑战性，因为故障可能涉及源代码、模型、数据、依赖项和执行环境。此外，不完整的错误报告由于遗漏了基本细节，进一步使复现复杂化。
method: RepGen通过上下文感知代码生成和迭代验证来复现DL错误。它首先探索代码库以构建学习增强的上下文，然后制定复现计划并生成候选脚本。RepGen使用静态检查和LLM反馈来改进候选脚本的正确性和相关性。该工具还可以准备执行环境，运行脚本，并根据报告的故障评估其输出。它提供交互式命令行界面和GitHub Action。
results: RepGen成功复现了106个真实世界DL错误中的85个（80.19%）。一项针对27名开发人员的对照研究显示，复现成功率提高了23.35%，复现时间减少了56.8%。
conclusion: RepGen作为一种通过上下文感知代码生成和迭代验证来复现深度学习错误的工具，在真实世界错误复现和提高开发人员效率方面表现出显著的有效性。

title: QUAL: Quantile Alignment Improves Zero-Shot Time-Series Foundation Models
authors: Junhyeok Kang, Sangjun Han, Jun Seo, Seunghan Lee, Jaehoon Lee, Dongwan Kang, Minjae Kim, Sungdong Yoo, Tae Yoon Lim, Hwanil Choi, Soonyoung Lee, Wonbin Ahn
abstract: Time-series foundation models (TSFMs) provide zero-shot forecasts for unseen series, but their accuracy varies across datasets. Combining several models can reduce this variability, yet zero-shot deployment provides no target labels for selecting or weighting them. We find that a model pool is useful not only as a final ensemble, but also as a probability reference for transforming each member forecast. Aligning quantiles through this pool-relative reference improves every member forecast in aggregate. Motivated by this finding, we propose QUAL (Quantile alignment), a simple label-free framework for improving and combining diverse TSFMs. QUAL first produces aligned member forecasts, then applies Huber aggregation and rearrangement to obtain a robust combined forecast without training or model modification. On GIFT-Eval, quantile alignment reduces average member MASE and CRPS by 7.4% and 9.8%. The full framework remains robust when weak forecasters enter a candidate pool whose quality cannot be verified in advance. Code is available at https://github.com/junhyeokkang/QUAL.
comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Foundation Models for Temporal Systems: From Forecasting to World Modeling
zh_title: QUAL：分位数对齐提升零样本时间序列基础模型
translation: 时间序列基础模型（TSFMs）为未见序列提供零样本预测，但其准确性因数据集而异。组合多个模型可以减少这种变异性，然而零样本部署不提供用于选择或加权它们的目标标签。我们发现，模型池不仅可以用作最终的集成，还可以用作转换每个成员预测的概率参考。通过该池相对参考对齐分位数，可以在总体上改善每个成员的预测。受此发现的启发，我们提出了QUAL（Quantile alignment），一个简单且无标签的框架，用于改进和组合多样化的TSFMs。QUAL首先产生对齐的成员预测，然后应用Huber聚合和重排以获得稳健的组合预测，而无需训练或模型修改。在GIFT-Eval上，分位数对齐使平均成员MASE和CRPS分别减少了7.4%和9.8%。当无法预先验证质量的弱预测器进入候选池时，整个框架仍然保持稳健。代码可在 https://github.com/junhyeokkang/QUAL 获取。
tldr: 提出了一种名为QUAL的无标签分位数对齐框架，无需训练即可显著提升并组合多个零样本时间序列基础模型的预测性能。
