The results reveal a consistent trade-off in which models that achieve high information preservation do so at the cost of sparsity, while models approaching the uniformity of an optimal random sparse code tend to sacrifice it. Competitive Sparse Codes, a biologically plausible approach, is the only architecture to occupy a region of near-maximal sparsity while retaining meaningful information preservation. These findings frame the simultaneous satisfaction of both factors as an open challenge for the field and provide a reusable evaluation framework for measuring progress toward it.

title: Optimal Average Distortion for Non-Expansive Embeddings of Euclidean Metrics into the Line: With applications to cut-matching games and vertex expansion
authors: Jack Spalding-Jamieson
abstract:
We show that any $n$-point Euclidean metric admits a non-expansive embedding into the line with average distortion at most $O\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}}\right)$, matching a known lower bound.
  We also present two applications of this result. First, we give a cut-player strategy with an optimal spectral guarantee for the undirected cut-matching game. Second, we give an improved spectral approximation for vertex expansion in high-degree graphs.

title: Epidemic Forecasting and Behavioral Response Estimation with a Behavior-Coupled SEIR Model
authors: Sungi Hong, Soham Das, Hossein Khazaei, Alfredo Garcia, Keith Paarporn, Ceyhun Eksin
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has exhibited multiple waves of infections, reflecting feedback between disease transmission and adaptive population behavior. Accurately predicting and understanding these dynamics remains a central challenge for epidemic modeling. In this paper, we develop a forecasting framework based on a Susceptible-Exposed-Infectious-Recovered (SEIR) model coupled with an evolutionary model of behavioral adaptation, in which population compliance with protective measures evolves in response to perceived infection risk and associated costs. We formulate forecasting as the estimation of behavioral incentive parameters that govern the coupled behavior-disease dynamics, using hospitalization time series data together with standard assumptions on disease-related parameters. Using the inferred parameters, we generate rolling monthly forecasts of infection levels and evaluate the approach on both synthetic data and hospitalization time series from multiple U.S. states (Texas, California, Colorado, and Arizona). The proposed framework provides a principled way to incorporate behavior-disease feedback into epidemic forecasting while yielding interpretable estimates of population-level incentives.
comment: 12 pages, 6 figures, 7 tables. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Computational Social Systems

title: Sensorium: An Open-Source Multimodal Data Collection and Curation Library for Embodied Surgical AI
authors: Lorenzo Mazza, Ariel Rodriguez, Stefanie Speidel
abstract: Embodied surgical AI requires reliable multimodal data, yet surgical data collection remains costly, difficult to repeat, and strongly dependent on the hardware setup. We present Sensorium, an open-source Python library for recording, processing, annotating, and curating multimodal surgical data from configurable robot and sensor streams using the Robot Operating System (ROS) and ROS2 middleware. The library combines operator-facing data acquisition, configurable processing, semantic annotation, and episodic dataset generation. We evaluate Sensorium across 1516 recordings of phantom, ex vivo, and in vivo porcine experiments involving multiple surgical tasks and sensing configurations, and report preliminary usability feedback.
comment: GenAI for Health Workshop @ NeurIPS 2026, Sydney

title: Optimizing Stochastic Policy Geometry for Few-Step Flow Reinforcement Learning
authors: Zhuguanyu Wu, Congjia Chen, Ruihao Gong, Yang Yong, Shiqiao Gu, Yi Xu, Xianglong Liu
abstract: Few-step flow models generate samples through a handful of large denoising transitions. Applying GRPO to such models requires introducing stochasticity into the denoising transitions, and when a single transition spans a wide range of noise levels, the choice of the resulting stochastic policy becomes a major factor in optimization. Recent constructions constrain the policy to preserve the target flow coefficients, but this constraint admits a family of policies and offers no criterion for choosing among them. We introduce Geo-FSRL (Geometry-Optimized Few-Step Reinforcement Learning), built on a selection principle: at a fixed conditioning state and timestep pair, choose the admissible policy that minimizes the conditional KL divergence induced by any given nonzero velocity-output update. Within a coefficient-preserving family of isotropic Gaussian transitions, this criterion reduces to minimizing a single scalar geometry factor that determines the conditional KL for every velocity-output update. The same factor governs velocity-space Fisher information and conditional transition log-likelihood-ratio variance. We derive the unique closed-form optimizer within this family, shared across all nonzero update magnitudes and directions, with transition coefficients determined by both the source and target noise levels. Because the minimized geometry factor still varies across timesteps, we further adopt gradient-scale matching from prior work and derive closed-form policy-gradient and KL weights that normalize explicit score scales and reference-KL curvature. Geo-FSRL trains on the original few-step schedule and retains the deterministic solver at inference. Our method achieves higher final reward scores than Flow-GRPO and Flow-CPS on both image generation and video generation models under the 4-step setting. Code is available at https://github.com/ModelTC/LightX2V/tree/main/lightx2v_rl

title: Aligning MLLMs with the Latent Structure of Human Cognition via Behavior-Derived Semantic Dimensions
authors: Ning E, Changde Du, Yizhuo Lu, Huiguang He
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have achieved impressive performance across a wide range of reasoning tasks, yet it remains unclear whether their internal representations and decision criteria align with the latent structure of human cognition. In this work, we propose a novel framework to align MLLMs with the multidimensional mental representations underlying human similarity judgements. We build on a previously established behavior-derived semantic embedding space, in which objects are represented along 66 interpretable dimensions derived from 4.70 million human Odd-One-Out (O1O) judgements. For each triplet, we infer the most salient decision dimension and convert it into a dimension-grounded linguistic rationale. This enables MLLMs to learn both the final choice and a justification consistent with the inferred behavioral criterion. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach improves model consistency with human similarity judgements while retaining competitive performance on standard multimodal benchmarks. Furthermore, using searchlight Representational Similarity Analysis (RSA) on an independent fMRI Natural Scenes Dataset (NSD), we observe increased representational alignment between model and human. Ultimately, our findings point to a data-driven route for incorporating human cognitive structure into MLLMs alignment. The code is available \href{https://github.com/ening-open/cogalign}{here}.

title: Chronos-2: A foundation model for multivariate time series forecasting
authors: Abdul Fatir Ansari, Oleksandr Shchur, Jaris Küken, Andreas Auer, Boran Han, Pedro Mercado, Syama Sundar Rangapuram, Huibin Shen, Lorenzo Stella, Xiyuan Zhang, Mononito Goswami, Shubham Kapoor, Danielle C. Maddix, Pablo Guerron, Florian Saupe, Markus Reichstein, Tony Hu, Junming Yin, Nick Erickson, Prateek Mutalik Desai, Hao Wang, Huzefa Rangwala, George Karypis, Yuyang Wang, Michael Bohlke-Schneider
abstract: Accurate forecasting with uncertainty quantification is critical in a variety of scientific applications ranging from epidemiology and economics to energy systems and earth sciences. Yet most forecasting models still need to be developed and trained separately for each domain-specific dataset. Time series foundation models (TSFMs) aim to remove this limitation and enable the application of the same model across domains through large-scale pretraining. However, most existing TSFMs treat each time series independently and therefore cannot model interactions among time series and external drivers. Here, we introduce Chronos-2, a foundation model for zero-shot forecasting that models the interactions between multivariate time series and heterogeneous covariates, which commonly arise in scientific applications. The model infers relationships among time series directly from historical context and generates probabilistic forecasts without task-specific treatment. Across various benchmarks, Chronos-2 achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on average by improving skill scores by 5.2 percentage points relative to the strongest baselines and increasing win rates by 10 percentage points. Chronos-2 is also computationally efficient, generating forecasts for 100 time series in under one second on a single mid-range GPU, 50x and 1000x faster end-to-end than the best task-specific point and probabilistic forecasters, respectively. In addition, we demonstrate its effectiveness in diverse scientific settings -- including infectious-disease forecasting, macroeconomic modeling, carbon-flux prediction, and runoff simulation -- where the model matches or surpasses specialized methods developed for each domain. These results show that a single pretrained model can capture structure shared across temporal systems.
comment: 41 pages, 9 figures. Extended version of the Chronos-2 technical report (arXiv:2510.15821), adding scientific case studies (epidemiology, macroeconomics, carbon flux, hydrology, hierarchical forecasting), additional baselines, ablation studies, and calibration analysis. Code: https://github.com/amazon-science/chronos-forecasting

title: A Robust High-order Approximation of the Gray Thermal Radiative Transfer Equations
authors: Jean-Luc Guermond, Wyatt M.R. Smith, Eric J. Tovar
abstract: We present a high-order, positivity preserving, and asymptotic preserving approximation of the gray radiative transfer equations. The time and space approximation is done using a diagonally-implicit Runge-Kutta method with stabilized, continuous finite elements, and the angular approximation uses the method of discrete ordinates. We detail a simple and robust inner/outer iteration strategy to solve these equations and prove that the proposed scheme is exactly conservative, independent of iterative tolerances. A maximum and minimum principle is enforced using a conservative redistribution limiting technique, and the method is demonstrated to be robust in the thick diffusion limit.

title: Robust Learning of Multi-Index Models under Logconcave Distributions via Weak Partial Learners
authors: Ilias Diakonikolas, Daniel M. Kane, Mingchen Ma
abstract:
We develop a new algorithmic framework for learning Boolean concept classes under logconcave distributions. Our framework applies to broad families of multi-index models and yields significantly faster robust learners than were previously known in these settings. It extends to partial classification and testable learning. Consequently, we obtain improved learners for several fundamental concept classes, including functions of halfspaces and multiclass linear classifiers, under logconcave marginals.
  Our starting point is a new boosting framework based on weak partial learners. Classical boosting approaches require often-intractable distribution-free weak learners or yield weak approximation guarantees. We show instead that weak learners for partial classification, where labels may be undefined on part of the domain, suffice for strong agnostic learning. The key challenge is that boosting requires a weak learner that succeeds under conditioned distributions that are not guaranteed to be logconcave. To address this, we develop a recursive moment-based partitioning procedure: given a logconcave distribution $X$ and a conditional version $X'$, we partition the space into polynomially many convex regions so that, on most regions, the low-degree moments of $X$ and $X'$ approximately agree. On each good region, a well-behaved multi-index model correlates with a low-degree polynomial, giving a weak hypothesis. Combining these hypotheses yields the required weak learner.
  A key ingredient of our approach is an efficient method for detecting moment discrepancy. Specifically, we show how to find a low-dimensional subspace that captures any non-trivial discrepancy between $X$ and $X'$, if one exists. Our approach combines spectral analysis of moment tensors with recent progress on isoperimetry for logconcave measures. This discrepancy-finding procedure may be of independent interest.

title: When Is a Game a Markov Decision Process? Correspondences Between Game Theory and Reinforcement Learning
authors: Eduardo C. Garrido-Merchán
abstract: Reinforcement learning and game theory describe the same object from two sides. Game theory says what a rational outcome of a strategic interaction is; reinforcement learning says how an agent could reach one through experience. The two literatures nevertheless keep separate vocabularies for identical structures, and the treatments that bridge them present the correspondence as analogy rather than theorem. This monograph supplies the theorems. A game is a Markov decision process in three distinct senses, and every table entry is labelled with the one that applies: a definitional identity, an exact reduction carried by a value- and solution-preserving map, or a structural analogy that fails under identifiable conditions. We take every standard class of game, from normal-form through repeated, stochastic, partially observable, extensive-form with imperfect information, Bayesian, graphical, Stackelberg, potential, coalitional, mean-field and evolutionary games, and identify for each the decision-theoretic model that reinforcement learning already studies under another name. The same treatment is applied to solution concepts: Nash equilibrium and the fixed point of the Bellman optimality operator, quantal response equilibrium and the soft Bellman operator, the Shapley value and credit assignment, Blackwell approachability and no-regret learning. We map each model class onto the training procedures sound for it and record the complexity of the associated solution problems. A final part collects the correspondences that do not hold: the non-stationarity that invalidates the independent-learner reduction, the impossibility results that forbid uncoupled convergence to Nash equilibrium, and the gap between the coarse correlated equilibria that no-regret self-play reaches and the correlated equilibria it is credited with.

title: Prune Gradually, Adapt Sparsely: Efficient Pruning of Large Language Models at Extreme Sparsity
authors: Jean Lucien Randrianantenaina, Hung Nguyen, Nasib Ullah, Jinbin Zhang, Nilesh Gupta, Inderjit S. Dhillon, Rohit Babbar
abstract: Weight pruning can reduce the storage and inference cost of large language models (LLMs), but preserving quality at high sparsity levels remains challenging. Existing methods face a quality-cost trade-off in this regime. One-shot pruning is cheap but degrades sharply as sparsity increases, even when followed by post-pruning recovery. A growing line of work instead optimizes the mask directly from the dense model under the end-to-end objective; among these methods, [Lee et al.,2026], the recent state of the art at extreme sparsity, reaches high quality but at the cost of model-sized optimizer state and auxiliary variables. To address this gap, we propose ETAPS, which prunes gradually and adapts sparsely: it tightens a global sparsity constraint in progressive stages while training a sparse delta with a small, fixed budget. Our key observation is that gradual weight removal keeps each pruning step small enough for sparse adaptation to compensate, allowing the adapted model to provide end-to-end gradients that guide the next pruning decision without model-sized optimizer state. Across six models from 125M to 13B parameters, ETAPS achieves lower perplexity than ELSA at every evaluated sparsity from 50% to 90%, with perplexity reductions of up to 42%. ETAPS is also far cheaper: at 90% sparsity, it prunes LLaMA2-7B on a single H200, where ELSA uses four, with $5.0\times$ smaller total persistent state and 49% fewer GPU-hours. Together, our findings point to a promising direction for achieving high quality in demanding regimes such as extreme sparsity at substantially lower cost.

title: When Does Test-Time Search Help World Action Models? An Empirical Audit of Candidate Selection and Simulator Integrity
authors: Jun Liu, Dajie Sun, Zhenglun Kong, Zhenjiang Fan, Peiyan Dong, Fan Yang, Wenbin Zhangg, Geng Yuan, Xue Lin, Yanzhi Wang, Dong Huang
abstract: World-action models increasingly apply test-time scaling, spending extra inference computation on candidate selection and adaptive allocation to improve control. Such gains are credible only when candidates carry exploitable signal, nominal compute savings become real speedup, and evaluation stays reliable. We audit all three on Cosmos Policy and RoboCasa with a premise-first, pre-registered methodology. On clean data, a learned value selector is 1.66 pp worse than random; a hindsight oracle gains only 1.40 pp, with an episode-level interval spanning zero; and 82% of states show identical candidate outcomes, leaving little selection headroom. Token pruning cuts per-forward FLOPs by up to 47% but yields at most a measured 1.15$\times$ end-to-end speedup on the deployed path (1.25$\times$ on a decode-excluded path), short of a 1.5$\times$ target, and our adaptive-allocation experiment is inconclusive under a power gate. We further identify and fix a silent rendering corruption whose rate rises sharply along compute-heavy planning paths while leaving the official direct-policy result unaffected, and release a detector, fix, and scripts. These findings show why test-time scaling should be audited as a chain of premises (decision signal, realized efficiency, evaluationintegrity) rather than by success rate alone. Conclusions are scoped to the tested configuration.

title: Model Checking for Metric Extensions of Monadic Second-Order Logic
authors: Dibyayan Chakraborty, Sebastian Ordyniak, Sebastian Siebertz
abstract:
Monadic second-order logic yields powerful algorithmic meta-theorems, but cannot express that a vertex set induces a shortest path. We study metric extensions of counting monadic second-order logic and identify structural parameters supporting efficient model checking, optimization, and counting.
  We show that shortest paths and equidistance guarded by geodesic cycles are definable in ordinary vertex-set MSO on graph classes of bounded cycle-basis length. This yields fixed-parameter tractable model checking for the corresponding extensions of CMSO2, parameterized by formula length and bag-connected treewidth, and of CMSO1, parameterized by formula length and geodesic cliquewidth: the sum of cliquewidth and cycle-basis length. The translations preserve free variables, yielding additive optimization and counting. Applications include Minimum Geodetic Set and Strong Metric Dimension for geodesic cliquewidth, and Minimum Isometric Path Partition for bag-connected treewidth.
  We also introduce restricted packing-covering templates that allow numerical distance thresholds to remain outside the parameter. For each fixed template, feasibility, additive vertex-weight optimization, and counting are fixed-parameter tractable in bag-connected treewidth. Applications include Distance-r Dominating Set, d-Scattered Set, and Minimum Eccentricity Shortest Path.
  Finally, we characterize bounded bag-connected treewidth and bounded geodesic cliquewidth through monadic dependence for the corresponding guarded logics. Unguarded distance comparisons have stricter structural boundaries: first-order model checking is AW[*]-complete already on uncolored caterpillars, and model checking a fixed existential monadic sentence is NP-complete on this class.

title: Language-Conditioned Behavioral Cloning for Autonomous Endoscope Guidance
authors: Ariel Rodriguez, Lorenzo Mazza, Ortrun Hellig, Alejandra Toscano, Rayan Younis, Stefanie Speidel
abstract: Automated endoscope guidance reduces the need for continuous manual camera control during minimally invasive surgery. However, the desired camera motion depends on the surgeon's immediate intentions and cannot always be inferred from the visual operative scene alone. We propose to automate the task using language-conditioned behavioral cloning; we define 6 clinically relevant guidance behaviors and collect 235 subtask demonstrations. In preliminary phantom experiments, our policy achieves 100% success on focus, overview, and stop, 80% on search-tip and follow-tip behaviors, and 50% on horizon leveling. These results demonstrate the feasibility of learning heterogeneous surgeon-requested camera behaviors with a single visuomotor policy, while the observed failure modes motivate future work on adding temporal context for more demanding guidance tasks.
comment: The Evolving Landscape of Surgical Robotics: Surgical Autonomy for Today and Tomorrow @ IROS 2026

title: New Lower Bounds for Private PAC Learning
authors: Prathamesh Dharangutte, Amartya Sanyal
abstract: We study realizable PAC learning under approximate differential privacy, and give a framework for proving lower bounds on its sample complexity. We construct classes with identical VC and Littlestone dimensions but different private sample complexities at common privacy and accuracy parameters, showing that these dimensions do not determine the sample complexity, even for improper learners. To address this we introduce the Independent Class Packing (ICP) parameter, the largest total sample complexity of classes in $\mathcal{G}$ that can be packed independently into a class $\mathcal{H}$, and prove that every $(\varepsilon, δ)$-DP, $(α, β)$-PAC learner for $\mathcal{H}$, possibly improper, uses $Ω\left(\mathrm{ICP}(\mathcal{H}, \mathcal{G})/(α\varepsilon)\right)$ examples. Using this framework we prove tight lower bounds for axis-aligned rectangles, union of intervals and linear subspaces and improved lower bounds for halfspaces and convex polygons. Finally we also show that for product classes, and more generally when the same classes pack into $\mathcal{H}$ and cover its domain so that target labels can be used directly, ICP characterizes private PAC sample complexity up to logarithmic factors.

title: Suspended-Fabric Robotic Manipulation Surfaces: Modelling, Design Space, and Multimodular Extensio
authors: Pratik Ingle, Jørn Lambertsen, Kasper Støy, Andres Faiña
abstract: Robotic Manipulation Surfaces (RMS) reposition objects by deforming the surface on which they rest. A recent class of RMS suspends a continuous fabric sheet from a sparse grid of vertical linear actuators lowering the actuator density of such surfaces but how to design such surfaces so that objects can be controlled everywhere on it, and how to extend it beyond a single module so that objects can pass between modules and achieve parallel, remain open. This paper presents a separable catenary model of the suspended sheet that is fast to compute and provides both the surface shape for given actuator heights and the actuator heights for a desired local slope. The closed form inverse lets a simple PID controller position objects on the sheet, and the model relates fabric length, module span and actuator stroke to the reachable workspace, yielding a minimum fabric length bound and design charts for these surfaces. The approach is then extended to a multimodular platform in which neighbouring modules share actuators. On a $2 \times 2$ prototype, we demonstrate that centimetre-scale objects are transferred between modules and positioned within 0.03 m over a $1 m^2$ workspace with only nine actuators, enabling multi-object manipulation and opening the way to parallel manipulation.

title: Design and Validation of a Robotic Knee Exoskeleton with Musculoskeletal Simulation-Derived Biological Torque Control
authors: Rajiv V. Joshi, Jimin An, Ilseung Park, Dawit Lee, Inseung Kang
abstract: Data-driven controllers have enabled lower-limb robotic exoskeletons to adapt assistance to the user across many tasks. A leading example is biological torque control, which estimates the user's own joint moment from onboard sensors and assists in proportion to that estimate. However, its estimators are trained on data recorded with the target device, so deploying the controller on new hardware requires collecting new data. Existing open-source efforts release hardware, software, or controllers separately, so this data collection must still be repeated on the assembled device. Here, we present an open-source knee exoskeleton, built from off-the-shelf components and widely available fabrication tools, with a biological torque controller derived entirely from simulation. A muscle-driven imitation policy reproduces squatting motions from an open biomechanics dataset, and the resulting knee moments are distilled into an estimator that uses only onboard sensors, so no training data are recorded on the device. In seven able-bodied participants, assistance reduced peak biological knee extension moment by 21.5% and peak vastus medialis activation by 26.7% during squatting, relative to squatting without the exoskeleton (p<0.05). Our results demonstrate that a biological torque controller derived from simulation can transfer to physical hardware without device-specific data collection. Because the hardware and training pipeline are released together, research groups can train and compare knee exoskeleton controllers on shared hardware without additional data collection overhead.

title: TwinPast: Benchmarking Historical Evidence Use in Streaming Video Understanding with Evidence Contrastive Video Pairs
authors: Haotian Yang, Yong Chen, Cheng Peng, Haobo Wang, Zhongle Xie, Xuanru Li, Gang Chen
abstract: High accuracy on streaming video benchmarks does not establish whether a model uses visual history. Our review of OVO-Bench and StreamingBench finds that recent frames suffice for 32% of sampled historical questions, while models also answer many questions correctly from the question and options alone. We introduce TwinPast to test whether answers correctly follow changes in history, using 350 human-reviewed video pairs spanning five historical tasks. Each pair holds the recent video context, question, and ordered options fixed while changing critical historical evidence and the correct answer. Each video is evaluated independently, and PairAcc requires correct answers for both histories. We evaluate 34 model and input configurations. For Qwen3-VL-8B and DeepSeek-Flash, historical inputs improve performance on TwinPast, reversing the recent-frame advantage on existing benchmarks. The strongest evaluated streaming system reaches 49.14% PairAcc, compared with 66.57-91.43% for the evaluated general-purpose models. This gap persists across all five tasks. Case studies further show that models select states from the wrong time or contradict recorded event order despite retaining the relevant evidence. These findings highlight the need to connect historical memory and retrieval with reasoning that uses evidence according to the question's temporal references and event relations.

title: FoAViS: Analyzing Learned Fixation Strategies in a Foveated Active Vision System
authors: Valentin Hassler, Jonathan Henrich, Yohaï-Eliel Berreby, Haoze Zhu, Alexander Ecker
abstract: Human vision is foveated and active: resolution is highest at the fovea and falls off towards the periphery, and fixations are actively directed to locations of interest. Building a machine system that processes information in the same way lets us study gaze behavior in a controlled setting where the system's components and objectives are known. The emergence of gaze characteristics can therefore be examined systematically, which may in turn inform our understanding of biological vision. This requires a model that can sample like the fovea, handle various tasks from classification to dense prediction, and be trained concurrently with a fixation policy. In our study, we present such a system and study its capabilities and the fixation policies that emerge from it. Our system, FoAViS, samples visual input by adopting the established log-polar foveation and accumulates information in a 2D spatial memory. Due to its 2D structure, the same memory can be read out globally for classification or densely for semantic segmentation, without any architectural change. Fixations are drawn from a 2D map by a policy trained concurrently with the task. We find that learned fixation policies select more informative, task-specific locations than non-learned heuristics. These policies also shape the task representations in a beneficial way: for both classification and segmentation, models trained concurrently with a policy outperform models trained with random locations, even when the latter are provided with learned scanpaths. Moreover, these scanpaths exhibit similarities to human gaze behavior by capturing aspects of empirical scanpath characteristics. Our work marks an important step away from standard passive, single-pass architectures, towards biologically grounded models of vision. It opens a path for studying goal-directed gaze behavior and information representation in the visual system.

title: ID2Pattern: Pretraining Generalizable Identity Behavior Patterns for Transaction Risk Foundation Models
authors: Ze Zhao, Haoyu Jiang, Weiyu Han, Ruobing Zuo, Xiao Tan, Shuai Chen, Tianyi Zhang
abstract: Large-scale behavioral pretraining offers a promising route to generalizable representations in online payment systems. However, high-cardinality identity fields such as card, device, and account IDs, though rich in behavioral signals, remain underexploited. Their continually growing vocabularies and limited semantic meaning make existing vocabulary-based and semantics-based encodings ill-suited. Their generalizable signal lies not in specific values, but in the identity behavior patterns they exhibit across a transaction sequence. Building on this insight, we propose ID2Pattern, a pretraining framework that brings these patterns into transaction foundation models. ID2Pattern first encodes identity fields with a Local Anonymous ID (LAID) tokenizer, which captures how each identity appears and recurs within the sequence, independent of its specific value. It then pretrains a multi-scale pattern codebook on unlabeled sequences, which abstracts LAID sequences into discrete behavior patterns for downstream prediction. Experiments on an industrial dataset with over 100M sequences and six public datasets show that ID2Pattern consistently outperforms strong baselines, improving industrial by 4.13% and public datasets by 8.83% on average. Notably, ID2Pattern remains equally effective even when all identity values are unseen during training, highlighting its potential to generalize to new users and markets.
zh_title: ID2Pattern：面向交易风险基础模型预训练可泛化的身份行为模式
translation: 大规模行为预训练为在线支付系统中获得可泛化表征提供了一条有前景的路径。然而，卡号、设备和账户ID等高基数身份字段虽然富含行为信号，却仍未得到充分利用。其不断增长的词表规模和有限的语义含义，使得现有的基于词表和基于语义的编码方法难以适用。这些字段的可泛化信号并不存在于特定的ID数值中，而在于它们在交易序列中所展现的身份行为模式。基于这一洞察，我们提出了 ID2Pattern 预训练框架，将此类模式引入交易基础模型。ID2Pattern 首先使用局部匿名ID（LAID）分词器对身份字段进行编码，在独立于具体ID值的情况下，捕获每个身份在序列中出现和重现的方式。随后，它在无标签序列上预训练一个多尺度模式码本，将 LAID 序列抽象为用于下游预测的离散行为模式。在包含超过1亿条序列的工业数据集和六个公开数据集上的实验表明，ID2Pattern 持续优于强基线模型，在工业数据集上平均提升4.13%，在公开数据集上平均提升8.83%。值得注意的是，即使在训练期间所有身份取值均未见过，ID2Pattern 依然同样有效，突显了其泛化至新用户和新市场的巨大潜力。
tldr: ID2Pattern 通过局部匿名ID和多尺度模式码本预训练，抽离具体ID值并建模交易序列中的身份行为模式，成功解决了高基数身份字段难以泛化的难题。
ai_comments: 该论文的核心创新在于跳出传统的“ID嵌入”和“语义文本化”框架，洞察到高基数身份字段的本质泛化特征在于序列内的复现行为模式而非具体数值，提出了局部匿名ID结合多尺度码本预训练的优雅方案，对工业级冷启动和风控迁移问题具有极高的实用价值；其局限在于摘要未披露多尺度码本的具体构建方式及长序列下的计算复杂度。
motivation: 在在线支付风控中，高基数身份字段（如卡号、设备ID）蕴含丰富行为信号，但由于词表持续膨胀且缺乏明确语义，传统的基于词表或语义的编码方式无法有效泛化；其真正的泛化价值存在于身份跨交易序列的行为出现模式中，而非具体的ID数值。
method: 提出 ID2Pattern 预训练框架：1）采用局部匿名ID（LAID）分词器，剥离具体ID数值，仅捕获序列中各身份的出现与重现动态；2）在无标注交易序列上预训练多尺度模式码本，将 LAID 序列离散化抽象为通用的行为模式供下游模型使用。
results: 在包含超1亿条序列的工业数据集上取得4.13%的平均提升，在6个公开数据集上平均提升8.83%；更重要的是，当所有身份取值在训练期完全未见过时，模型效果依然保持一致有效。
conclusion: ID2Pattern 能够有效利用无标签交易序列预训练出通用的身份行为模式，使交易风险基础模型即使在面对未见过的全新身份时也能保持高精度，展现出强大的跨用户和跨市场泛化能力。

title: DAMI: Dual-Axis Memory Initialization for Enhanced Long-Context Retrieval in Gated Linear Attention
authors: Zhangchi Feng, Harry Jiang, Yangyifei Luo, Ray Zhang, Richong Zhang
abstract: Linear attention scales linearly with sequence length, but its finite-state memory can limit long-context retrieval. In gated linear recurrences, memory retention depends on state decay, which is shaped jointly by gate parameters A_log and dt_bias and by input activations. In controlled Gated DeltaNet (GDN) experiments, both parameters remain highly correlated with their initial values after training, highlighting the importance of initialization. Therefore, we introduce Dual-Axis Memory Initialization (DAMI), which jointly configures these parameters before training. DAMI assigns geometric timescales across heads for varied retrieval distances and a low-high-low input-sensitivity profile across layers. A small activation sample calibrates the GDN-family implementation to match both behavioral targets without adding trainable parameters. Across GDN, KDA, GDN2, Mamba-2, and RWKV-7, DAMI improves average RULER-style retrieval accuracy by 5.29 to 16.71 percentage points over the corresponding random-initialization baselines. Performance on language modeling, commonsense reasoning, and 2K real-world retrieval remains broadly comparable to those baselines. Our code is available at https://speedai.com/research/dami.
zh_title: DAMI：用于增强门控线性注意力中长文本检索的双轴内存初始化
translation: 线性注意力随序列长度线性缩放，但其有限状态记忆可能会限制长文本检索。在门控线性递归中，记忆保持取决于状态衰减，该衰减由门参数 $A_{log}$、$\text{dt\_bias}$ 以及输入激活共同决定。在受控的 Gated DeltaNet (GDN) 实验中，这两个参数在训练后与其初始值保持高度相关，突显了初始化的重要性。因此，我们引入了双轴内存初始化 (DAMI)，在训练前联合配置这些参数。DAMI 为不同的检索距离在各个头上分配了几何时间尺度，并在各层之间分配了低-高-低的输入敏感度曲线。一小批激活样本可将 GDN 家族的实现校准为匹配这两个行为目标，且无需增加可训练参数。在 GDN、KDA、GDN2、Mamba-2 和 RWKV-7 中，与相应的随机初始化基线相比，DAMI 将平均 RULER 风格的检索准确率提高了 5.29 到 16.71 个百分点。在语言建模、常识推理和 2K 真实世界检索上的性能与这些基线大致相当。我们的代码可在 https://speedai.com/research/dami 获取。
tldr: 提出了一种名为DAMI的双轴内存初始化方法，通过联合配置门参数，在不增加训练参数的情况下显著提升了线性注意力模型的长文本检索能力。
ai_comments: 该论文针对线性注意力机制中有限状态内存限制长文本检索的问题，提出了双轴内存 initialization (DAMI) 方法。其创新之处在于通过联合配置门参数 A_log 和 dt_bias 来实现几何时间尺度和输入敏感性配置文件，无需增加可训练参数，显著提升了长文本检索能力。
motivation: 线性注意力随序列长度呈线性扩展，但其有限状态内存限制了长文本检索能力；在门控线性递归中，内存保留取决于状态衰减，该衰减由门参数和输入激活共同决定，且实验表明训练后这些参数与初始值高度相关，凸显了初始化的重要性。
method: 引入双轴内存初始化（DAMI），在训练前联合配置门参数 A_log 和 dt_bias，跨注意力头分配几何时间尺度以适应不同的检索距离，并在层间实现低-高-低的输入敏感性配置。利用小样本激活校准GDN系列实现，不增加可训练参数。
results: 在GDN、KDA、GDN2、Mamba-2和RWKV-7等模型中，DAMI将平均RULER风格的检索准确率较随机初始化基线提升了5.29至16.71个百分点，同时在语言建模、常识推理和2K真实世界检索上的性能保持相当水平。
conclusion: DAMI 是一种有效且通用的长文本检索增强方法，能够在不影响语言建模和常识推理性能的前提下，大幅提升线性注意力及状态空间模型的长文本检索准确率。

title: MoETok: Sparse Expert Routing for 1D Visual Tokenizers
authors: Jiahao Guo, Bao Tang, Haoxiang Cao, Jingfeng Yao, Bo Li, Wenyu Liu, Kun Gai, Changqian Yu, Xinggang Wang
abstract: Modern visual tokenizers aim to preserve fine-grained visual details while learning high-level semantic representations for downstream generation and understanding. Query-based 1D visual tokenizers encode images into flexible latent sequences, yet how individual learnable queries gather and encode image information remains poorly understood. We reveal that these queries spontaneously develop complementary roles under semantic supervision: a small set of Content queries captures high-level semantic information, while a larger set of Detail queries preserves fine-grained visual details for reconstruction. To adapt token processing to these heterogeneous roles, we introduce MoETok, a 1D visual tokenizer that routes tokens through sparsely activated experts. Jointly optimized with reconstruction and semantic objectives, the router learns role-specialized processing paths adapted to each token's representation. Across model scales and token budgets, MoETok consistently improves reconstruction, semantic representation, and autoregressive generation over dense tokenizers under matched supervision and active computation. On ImageNet, it combines strong reconstruction and semantic representation with state-of-the-art class-conditional generation within the 1D tokenizer family. We further validate MoETok at scale in a unified autoregressive model jointly trained for understanding and generation with a next-token cross-entropy objective. The resulting model combines competitive visual understanding with state-of-the-art generation among unified discrete models, matching or surpassing diffusion-based models such as BAGEL and Qwen-Image on benchmarks including DPG-Bench (87.61), GenEval2 (40.04 GM), and WISE (0.49).
zh_title: MoETok: 1D视觉分词器的稀疏专家路由
translation: 现代视觉分词器旨在保留细粒度视觉细节，同时学习用于下游生成和理解的高级语义表示。基于查询的1D视觉分词器将图像编码为灵活的潜在序列，但单个可学习查询如何收集和编码图像信息仍不甚明了。我们揭示了这些查询在语义监督下自发地发展出互补的角色：一小组内容查询捕获高级语义信息，而更大一组细节查询保留细粒度视觉细节用于重建。为了使令牌处理适应这些异构角色，我们引入了MoETok，一个1D视觉分词器，它通过稀疏激活的专家路由来处理令牌。与重建和语义目标联合优化，路由器学习针对每个令牌表示的角色专业化处理路径。在模型规模和令牌预算方面，MoETok始终改进了重建、语义表示和自回归生成，优于匹配监督和活跃计算下的密集分词器。在ImageNet上，它结合了强大的重建和语义表示，并在1D分词器家族中实现了最先进的类别条件生成。我们进一步在一个统一的自回归模型中大规模验证了MoETok，该模型通过下一个令牌交叉熵目标共同训练用于理解和生成。由此产生的模型结合了有竞争力的视觉理解和在统一离散模型中最先进的生成，在DPG-Bench (87.61)、GenEval2 (40.04 GM)和WISE (0.49)等基准测试中匹配或超越了基于扩散的模型，如BAGEL和Qwen-Image。
tldr: MoETok是一种1D视觉分词器，通过稀疏激活的专家路由来处理图像信息。它发现查询会自发地发展出内容查询和细节查询的互补角色。MoETok在重建、语义表示和自回归生成方面优于密集分词器，并在ImageNet上实现了最先进的性能，同时在统一的自回归模型中取得了有竞争力的视觉理解和最先进的生成效果。
ai_comments: MoETok的创新点在于揭示了1D视觉分词器中查询的自发角色分化，并据此设计了稀疏专家路由机制。这种机制有效地适应了不同类型视觉信息（语义和细节）的处理需求，通过有选择地激活专家网络，提高了模型的效率和性能。其在多个视觉任务上取得的SOTA成果，证明了稀疏专家路由在视觉分词领域的巨大潜力，为未来高效、多功能的视觉表示学习提供了新思路。
motivation: 现代视觉分词器旨在保留细粒度视觉细节，同时学习用于下游生成和理解的高级语义表示。然而，1D视觉分词器中可学习查询如何收集和编码图像信息仍不甚明了。
method: 本文引入了MoETok，一种1D视觉分词器，它通过稀疏激活的专家路由来处理令牌。它与重建和语义目标联合优化，路由器学习针对每个令牌表示的角色专业化处理路径。研究发现，查询会自发地发展出互补的角色：少量内容查询捕获高级语义信息，而大量细节查询保留细粒度视觉细节用于重建。
results: MoETok在模型规模和令牌预算方面始终改进了重建、语义表示和自回归生成，优于匹配监督和活跃计算下的密集分词器。在ImageNet上，它结合了强大的重建和语义表示，并在1D分词器家族中实现了最先进的类别条件生成。在一个为理解和生成共同训练的统一自回归模型中，MoETok结合了有竞争力的视觉理解和在统一离散模型中最先进的生成，在DPG-Bench (87.61)、GenEval2 (40.04 GM)和WISE (0.49)等基准测试中匹配或超越了基于扩散的模型。
conclusion: MoETok通过引入稀疏专家路由机制，有效解决了1D视觉分词器中查询角色不明确的问题，显著提升了视觉重建、语义理解和生成任务的性能，并在多个基准测试中达到了或超越了现有先进模型水平。

title: AutoAnalysis: An automated, self-updating meta-analysis of human-AI collaboration
authors: Michelle Vaccaro, Abdullah Almaatouq, Thomas W. Malone
abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (AI) becomes more capable and widely used, understanding when and how humans should work with these systems is becoming increasingly important. However, the empirical evidence in this space offers conflicting recommendations, which leaves individuals and organizations without clear guidance on when to combine human and AI capabilities. Existing meta-analyses can help reconcile these findings, but they require substantial manual effort and cannot readily incorporate new evidence as it emerges. To address this challenge, we introduce AutoAnalysis: an automated, self-updating meta-analysis of when humans and AI work better together, and when they work better alone. AutoAnalysis' most recent run synthesizes 1,955 effect sizes from 420 papers. Across this body of work, we found that, on average, human-AI combinations performed significantly better than humans alone, but they performed significantly worse than the better of humans or AI alone. These findings highlight the important distinction between improving human performance and achieving human-AI synergy and underscore the need to evaluate collaboration against both human and AI performance alone. As new studies emerge, AutoAnalysis will integrate their findings into the meta-analysis, providing cumulative evidence about when humans and AI perform better together and how human-AI performance varies across AI agents, tasks, and processes.
comment: Please visit auto-analysis.dev to explore the data and view the most recent results
zh_title: AutoAnalysis：一项关于人机协作的自动化、自我更新的元分析
translation: 随着生成式人工智能（AI）变得越来越强大和广泛使用，理解人类何时以及如何与这些系统协同工作变得日益重要。然而，这一领域的实证证据给出了相互冲突的建议，导致个人和组织在何时结合人类与AI能力方面缺乏清晰的指导。现有的元分析虽然可以帮助协调这些发现，但它们需要大量的手工努力，且无法随着新证据的出现而随时整合。为了应对这一挑战，我们推出了AutoAnalysis：一个自动化、自我更新的元分析系统，旨在研究人类与AI何时共同工作得更好，何时各自工作得更好。AutoAnalysis最近的一次运行综合了来自420篇论文的1,955个效应量。在这些研究中，我们发现平均而言，人机组合的表现明显优于单纯的人类，但明显逊色于人类或AI中表现更好的一方。这些发现突显了提升人类表现与实现人机协同之间的重要区别，并强调了对照人类和AI单独表现来评估协作的必要性。随着新研究的出现，AutoAnalysis将把它们的发现整合到元分析中，提供关于人类与AI何时共同表现更好以及人机表现如何随AI智能体、任务和流程而变化的累积证据。
tldr: 本文推出了AutoAnalysis——一个自动更新的人机协作元分析系统，发现虽然人机组合优于人类自身，但仍不及人类与AI中的最优秀者。
ai_comments: AutoAnalysis 填补了现有元分析无法实时更新和耗费大量人工的空白，通过自动化和持续更新的机制，为理解人机协作提供了规模化且动态的实证视角。该研究不仅对人机协作的有效性给出了全局评估，其方法论对于其他快速发展的学术领域也具有重要的参考价值。
motivation: 随着生成式AI的普及，关于人机协作效果的实证研究层出不穷但结论相互冲突，而传统的元分析需要大量人工且无法随新证据实时更新。因此，需要一个自动化且自我更新的元分析系统来提供清晰、累积的指导。
method: 开发了AutoAnalysis自动化、自我更新的元分析系统，综合了来自420篇论文的1,955个效应量进行定量合成与持续追踪。
results: 最新运行结果表明：平均而言，人机组合的表现明显优于单独的人类，但明显逊色于人类或AI中表现更好的一方。这凸显了提升人类表现与实现人机协同之间的重要区别。
conclusion: 人机协作的平均表现优于单纯的人类，但逊色于单独的最优方（人类或AI），这强调了在人机协作研究中区分性能提升与真正协作协同的重要性。AutoAnalysis系统将持续提供动态、累积的实证证据。

title: Less Loss, Fixed Weights: Logit Corrections for Forgetting
authors: Hanyu Yang
abstract: When a language model is fine-tuned to follow instructions, or further pretrained on a new subject, it often gets worse at predicting standard web text. This is known as "forgetting." We ask whether this loss can be undone by simple, fixed adjustments to the model's final token predictions. Across 14 pairs of base and derived models, from 1B to 7B parameters, we fitted a fixed bonus or penalty for each token (a vocabulary bias), alone or together with a temperature. On text held out from correction fitting, the largest top-4K bias recovery estimate is under 10%, with loss conditional on the retained vocabulary. Combining the bias with a temperature recovers up to 36%. Models further pretrained on math lose the most and recover almost nothing. Finally, in a controlled simulation where a model is damaged at random, with no planted bias or temperature change, the bias-plus-temperature fix still recovers 29%. Most of the real-model loss increase stays out of reach of our restricted fits.
comment: 8 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables. Code and data: https://github.com/SeverinVisionary/prior-shift-diagnostic
zh_title: 更少的损失，固定的权重：用于遗忘的对数修正
translation: 当语言模型被微调以遵循指令，或在一个新主题上进一步预训练时，它预测标准网络文本的能力往往会变差。这被称为“遗忘”。我们探讨了这种损失是否可以通过对模型最终token预测进行简单、固定的调整来撤销。在14对1B到7B参数的基础模型和派生模型中，我们为每个token拟合了固定的奖励或惩罚（词表偏置），并单独或结合温度进行了调整。在从修正拟合中留出的文本上，最大的前4K偏置恢复估计低于10%（基于保留词表的条件损失）。将偏置与温度结合最多可以恢复36%。进一步在数学上进行预训练的模型损失最大，几乎无法恢复。最后，在一个随机损坏模型但没有植入偏置或温度变化的受控模拟中，偏置加温度的修正仍然恢复了29%。真实模型大部分的损失增加超出了我们受限拟合的触及范围。
tldr: 通过固定的词表偏置和温度调整来修正语言模型微调带来的遗忘，效果非常有限，大部分损失无法恢复。
ai_comments: 本文探讨了通过固定权重对数修正来恢复语言模型微调或增量预训练带来的遗忘问题，方法简单但发现大部分真实模型的性能损失无法通过这种受限的修正恢复，对理解模型遗忘机制有重要启示。
motivation: 研究语言模型在进行指令微调或新领域预训练时常出现的“遗忘”现象（即预测标准网络文本能力变差），探究这种损失是否可以通过对模型最终token预测进行简单、固定的调整来撤销。
method: 跨14对基础模型和派生模型（1B至7B参数），为每个token拟合固定的奖励或惩罚（词表偏置），单独或结合温度调节，并在留存文本上进行评估和模拟实验。
results: 仅使用词表偏置的恢复率不到10%，结合温度调节最多可恢复36%；在数学预训练模型上几乎无法恢复；随机损坏模拟实验中可恢复29%。大部分真实模型的损失无法通过这种受限拟合恢复。
conclusion: 简单的词表偏置和温度调节仅能恢复一小部分语言模型因微调或预训练导致的遗忘损失，说明遗忘主要发生在更深层次的表征中，无法仅通过最终的对数矫正来轻易撤销。

title: TradeWar: A Benchmark for Execution-Grounded Trade Negotiation with Adaptive LLM Agents
authors: Xiangyu Kong, Ruirui Yang, Xia Hou
abstract: Multi-turn negotiation remains a challenging problem for large language model (LLM) agents. While LLMs can conduct natural-language dialogue, existing benchmarks predominantly assess only agreement rates, overlooking whether negotiated commitments actually create value once executed. To address this gap, we introduce TradeWar, a multi-country simulation benchmark that translates negotiation dialogues into concrete tariff and trade-share policies, enforces capacity and network constraints during settlement, and evaluates outcomes via an Economic Health Index (EHI). To solve this execution-grounded task, we propose TACTIC (Trade-aware Adaptive Consolidation and Theory-of-mind for International Commerce), an agent that iteratively refines its negotiation strategy across episodes-without updating base LLM weights-by leveraging prior experience, opponent behavior, and past settlement outcomes. Despite using zero-shot chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting, PromptLLM attains a 75% agreement rate but only 57.1 final EHI (*100), whereas TACTIC reaches 68.8. Across 20 sequential episodes and three seeds, TACTIC's final EHI improves from 58.2 to 73.2, compared with 65.2 for an ablation without cross-episode updates. Under technology-controls and energy-crisis shocks, TACTIC also exhibits smaller performance degradation than PromptLLM and MemoryLLM. These results indicate that CoT deliberation and interaction memory alone do not fully address delayed execution feedback, whereas settlement-grounded adaptation improves long-horizon negotiation in TradeWar.

title: GeoFlip: Benchmarking Geometry-Sensitive Physics in Video Generation
authors: Yuqi Li, Junming Liu, Bowen Hu, Ruize Niu, Huiran Duan, Yingli Tian, Hao Wu
abstract: Video generation models synthesize realistic motion, but can they respond correctly to changes in initial geometry? We introduce GeoFlip, a video generation benchmark centered on physical outcome flips induced by geometry. With shared physical settings and textual prompts held fixed, GeoFlip applies controlled interventions to support extent, object placement, and mechanism configuration, constructing paired scenes with contrasting reference events, such as remaining stable versus falling or tipping. These pairs test whether models translate geometric differences in the first frame into correct physical evolution. The benchmark comprises 482 scene pairs and 964 reference videos across six physical categories, with reference outcomes established through procedural scene construction, physics simulation, and numerical validation and verification of physical events. We evaluate 16 models for image to video generation along three dimensions: event correctness, structural integrity, and similarity to reference videos. We examine evaluation consistency with independent vision language judges. On the 442 conditions shared by all models, the highest event correctness averaged across tasks is 27.98%, revealing substantial limitations in physical generation conditioned on geometry. Model strengths vary across physical mechanisms, and the three evaluation dimensions capture distinct capabilities. Typical failures include ignoring geometric changes, generating incorrect object motion, bending rigid objects, and introducing additional components. Rank correlations between judges reach 0.906 for event correctness and 0.929 for structural integrity. By combining controlled geometric interventions, verifiable physical references, and multidimensional evaluation, GeoFlip assesses progress from visual realism toward physical consistency conditioned on geometry.
zh_title: GeoFlip：视频生成中几何敏感物理特性的基准测试
translation: 视频生成模型可以合成逼真的运动，但它们能够正确响应初始几何结构的变化吗？我们介绍了GeoFlip，这是一个以几何引起的物理结果翻转为核心的视频生成基准。在保持共享物理设置和文本提示不变的情况下，GeoFlip对范围、物体放置和机构配置应用受控干预，构建了具有对比参考事件的成对场景，例如保持稳定与跌落或倾斜。这些对测试了模型是否能将第一帧中的几何差异转化为正确的物理演化。该基准包括482个场景对和964个参考视频，涵盖六个物理类别，其参考结果通过程序化场景构建、物理模拟以及物理事件的数值验证和核实确立。我们从三个维度评估了16个图生视频模型：事件正确性、结构完整性以及与参考视频的相似性，并检验了独立视觉语言裁判的评估一致性。在所有模型共享的442个条件下，跨任务平均的最高事件正确性为27.98%，这揭示了在以几何为条件的物理生成方面的重大局限性。模型优势因物理机制而异，三个评估维度捕捉到了不同的能力。典型失败包括忽略几何变化、生成不正确的物体运动、弯曲刚性物体以及引入额外的组件。裁判之间的秩相关性在事件正确性上达到了0.906，在结构完整性上达到了0.929。通过结合受控的几何干预、可验证的物理参考和多维评估，GeoFlip评估了从视觉真实感向以几何为条件的物理一致性的进展。
tldr: 本文提出了GeoFlip基准，用于测试视频 generation 模型根据初始几何变化预测物理结果的能力，结果发现现有模型在此方面的表现普遍较差。
ai_comments: GeoFlip是一个填补当前视频生成模型在几何敏感物理推理方面空白的重要基准。该研究通过受控的几何干预和严格的物理模拟验证，揭示了现有顶尖视频生成模型在理解和模拟基本物理规律方面的严重不足（最高事件正确率仅为27.98%），为未来物理一致的视频生成研究指明了方向。
motivation: 尽管视频生成模型能够合成逼真的运动，但它们是否能够正确响应初始几何结构的变化尚不明确，因此需要一个专门的基准来评估模型对几何敏感物理规律的理解和生成能力。
method: 引入GeoFlip基准，通过对初始帧的范围、物体放置和机构配置施加受控的几何干预，构建具有对比参考事件的成对场景（包含482个场景对和964个参考视频）；利用程序化场景构建、物理模拟和数值验证来确立参考结果；评估并分析了16个图生视频模型在事件正确性、结构完整性和参考相似性三个维度上的表现。
results: 在所有模型共享的442个条件中，任务平均最高事件正确性仅为27.98%；模型在不同物理机制上的表现各异，典型失败包括忽视几何变化、生成错误的物体运动、使刚性物体弯曲以及引入额外组件。
conclusion: GeoFlip基准测试表明，现有的视频生成模型在响应初始几何变化并正确模拟物理演化方面存在显著局限性，突出了视觉真实感与真正物理一致性之间的差距。

title: SecPO: Principled Adversarial Training for Prompt Injection Security
authors: Sizhe Chen, Yibo Peng, Jaewon Chang, Chawin Sitawarin, David Wagner
abstract: Recognized as a top threat to AI agents, prompt injection allows instructions from untrusted data (email, documents, websites) to manipulate the agent's operation. The existing best-defended LLM, Meta-SecAlign, is trained with the DPO loss but still suffers from attack success rates (ASRs) approaching 100% under adaptive prompt injections. One reason is that DPO anchors the model around the undefended reference model, which is insecure. We show an idealized reference model---an injection-invariant, utility-preserving oracle---can nevertheless be approximated, as its output distribution in training is interestingly accessible. This new observation motivates a theoretically principled SecPO loss. Another Meta-SecAlign shortcoming is that it trains on weak simulated attacks. We implement an efficient adversarial training (AT) pipeline that synthesizes strong injected inputs (best@240), and train the model on them. Our AT reduces ASRs by 1.5-14.5$\times$ across three SoTA adaptive attacks, compared with Meta-SecAlign; the SecPO loss reduces them by a further 2.4-4.6$\times$ compared with using DPO loss. In agentic workflows, our SecPO + AT Qwen3.6-27B is much more secure than Meta-SecAlign: 8.8% vs. 78.8% AgentDojo ASR@800 under the AttackerMovesSecond attack. Moreover, our defended model shows no noticeable reduction in benign utility in nine benchmarks covering agentic tool calling, instruction following, science, and math. We release our $\href{//github.com/Sizhe-Chen/SecPO}{\text{code}}$, $\href{//huggingface.co/datasets/Sizhe-Chen/Qwen3.6-27B-Instruct-SecPO-trainset}{\text{training data}}$ (with optimized injections from AT), and $\href{//huggingface.co/Sizhe-Chen/Qwen3.6-27B-Instruct-SecPO}{\text{model}}$.
zh_title: SecPO：基于原则的对抗训练以实现提示注入安全性
translation:
SecPO：基于原则的对抗训练以实现提示注入安全性

摘要：提示注入被认为是AI代理面临的头号威胁，它允许来自不受信任数据（电子邮件、文档、网站）的指令操纵代理的操作。现有防御最好的大型语言模型（LLM）Meta-SecAlign，尽管使用DPO损失进行训练，但在自适应提示注入下，其攻击成功率（ASR）仍接近100%。一个原因是DPO将模型锚定在不安全的未防御参考模型上。我们展示了一个理想化的参考模型——一个注入不变、实用性保持的预言机——尽管其在训练中的输出分布有趣地可访问，但仍可以被近似。这一新观察促使我们提出了一个理论上基于原则的SecPO损失。Meta-SecAlign的另一个缺点是它在弱模拟攻击下进行训练。我们实现了一个高效的对抗训练（AT）流程，合成强大的注入输入（best@240），并用它们训练模型。与Meta-SecAlign相比，我们的对抗训练将三种最先进的自适应攻击的ASR降低了1.5-14.5倍；与使用DPO损失相比，SecPO损失进一步将其降低了2.4-4.6倍。在代理工作流中，我们的SecPO + AT Qwen3.6-27B比Meta-SecAlign安全得多：在AttackerMovesSecond攻击下，AgentDojo ASR@800分别为8.8% vs. 78.8%。此外，我们防御后的模型在九个涵盖代理工具调用、指令遵循、科学和数学的基准测试中，良性实用性没有明显下降。我们发布了我们的代码、训练数据（包含来自AT的优化注入）和模型。
tldr: SecPO提出了一种新的损失函数和对抗训练方法，显著提高了大型语言模型（LLM）抵御提示注入攻击的能力，同时保持了良性实用性。
ai_comments: 本文在解决LLM提示注入安全这一关键问题上取得了显著进展。其创新点在于提出了理论上更严谨的SecPO损失，通过近似理想预言机来避免现有DPO损失的局限性，并结合了高效的对抗训练来生成更强大的攻击样本，从而提升了模型的鲁棒性。该研究对于提高AI代理在现实世界应用中的安全性具有重要意义，并且通过开源代码和模型，促进了社区的进一步研究。
motivation: 现有的最佳防御LLM（Meta-SecAlign）在面对自适应提示注入时攻击成功率接近100%，因为它使用DPO损失将模型锚定在不安全的参考模型上，并且依赖于弱模拟攻击进行训练。
method: 1. 提出了一种理论上基于原则的SecPO损失，通过近似一个理想化的、注入不变且实用性保持的预言机，其输出分布在训练中可访问。2. 实施了一个高效的对抗训练（AT）流程，合成强大的注入输入（best@240）并用它们训练模型。
results: 1. 与Meta-SecAlign相比，对抗训练将三种最先进的自适应攻击的攻击成功率降低了1.5-14.5倍。2. SecPO损失在对抗训练的基础上，进一步将攻击成功率降低了2.4-4.6倍。3. 在Agentic工作流中，SecPO + AT Qwen3.6-27B的安全性远高于Meta-SecAlign（AttackerMovesSecond攻击下AgentDojo ASR@800分别为8.8% vs. 78.8%）。4. 防御后的模型在九个涵盖代理工具调用、指令遵循、科学和数学的基准测试中，良性实用性没有明显下降。
conclusion: SecPO通过结合理论上基于原则的损失函数和高效的对抗训练，显著提高了LLM抵御提示注入攻击的安全性，同时保持了其在多种任务上的实用性。

title: TurnTurk-GPT: Text-Based Turn-Taking Prediction for Turkish
authors: Ahmet Tuğrul Bayrak, Fatma Nur Korkmaz, Nur Yağmur Tuncer, Mustafa Sertaç Türkel
abstract: This paper presents TurnTurk-GPT, a text-based turn-taking predictor for Turkish obtained by fine-tuning a Turkish GPT-2 model with the TurnGPT objective on synthetic and real dialogue, and evaluates it on real Turkish conversation against rule baselines, a zero-shot Turkish language model and a widely used multilingual end-of-turn detector. Evaluation uses word-level decision points on unpunctuated, lower-cased text approximating the output of streaming speech recognisers, recording-disjoint and speaker-disjoint folds, nested threshold selection and paired cluster bootstrap tests. TurnTurk-GPT outperforms the multilingual detector under both recording-disjoint and speaker-disjoint evaluation. It outperforms the zero-shot language model only when the test speakers occur in training; on unseen speakers the two are statistically indistinguishable. Removing the suffixes of the turn-final word reduces AP by up to 44%, against 2% for a sentence-internal word, locating the Turkish end-of-turn cue in verb-final morphology. Synthetic dialogue alone yields the weakest trained model, and when a speaker pauses the zero-shot and multilingual baselines remain close to chance. The model and the evaluation protocol are publicly released.

title: The C-3PO Framework: Algorithms for $\#\mathrm{BIS}$-Hard Problems on Graphs with Low Threshold Rank or High Girth
authors: Ijay Narang
abstract:
We give approximate counting and sampling algorithms for spin models on graphs of low threshold rank or high girth. Given any $n$-vertex graph $G$, let $k_η= k_η(G)$ count normalized-Laplacian eigenvalues strictly below $η$. For $\varepsilon > 0$, an $\varepsilon$-approximate counting algorithm outputs an estimate $\widehat Z$ of the partition function $Z$ satisfying $(1-\varepsilon)Z\le\widehat Z\le(1+\varepsilon)Z$ with probability at least $3/4$. An $\varepsilon$-approximate sampling algorithm outputs a configuration whose distribution is within total variation distance $\varepsilon$ of the target distribution. We give the following results:
  (a) Ferromagnetic Potts. Fix $q\ge2$ and $η\in(0,1]$. There exists $β_0(q,η)$ such that, for every inverse temperature $β\geβ_0$, the zero-field $q$-state Potts model admits approximate counting and sampling algorithms: (i) On arbitrary graphs in time $\exp(O(k_η))\operatorname{poly}(n,1/\varepsilon).$ (ii) Fix $Δ\ge 3$. On $Δ$-regular graphs of girth $g$ in time $\exp(O(n e^{-g})) \operatorname{poly}(n,1/\varepsilon).$
  (b) Bipartite hard-core. Fix $Δ\ge3$ and $η\in(0,1]$. There exists $λ_0(Δ,η)$ such that, for every fugacity $λ\geλ_0$, the hard-core model admits approximate counting and sampling: (i) On $Δ$-regular vertex-transitive bipartite graphs in time $\exp(O (k_η))\operatorname{poly}(n,1/\varepsilon).$ (ii) On $Δ$-regular bipartite graphs of girth $g$ in $\exp(O(n e^{- g}))\operatorname{poly}(n,1/\varepsilon).$
  All four results follow from verifying the hypotheses of a new framework we call C-3PO. At a high level, the C-3PO algorithm proceeds by enumerating small cuts and reconstructing the original measure through cluster expansions. Underlying the algorithm is an improvement of subspace enumeration methods via active regression.

title: 3SUM Made Simpler (Without Matrix Multiplication), $k$-SUM Hypothesis Refuted for Odd $k$, and Real 3SUM/APSP Derandomized
authors: Timothy M. Chan, Reina Itakura, Zhiyuan Ma, Yuancheng Yu
abstract:
Recently, a truly subquadratic algorithm for the 3SUM problem and a truly subcubic algorithm for the all-pairs shortest paths (APSP) problem were found by Anthropic, as reported by Alman and Vassilevska Williams (2026). These algorithms relied on a new subroutine for rectangular matrix multiplication with selected output entries, which was obtained by modifying known matrix multiplication techniques of Schönhage (1981) and Coppersmith (1982).
  1. We present a different truly subquadratic randomized algorithm for 3SUM for integer inputs. It completely avoids the use of matrix multiplication but instead modifies known dynamic programming algorithms for subset convolution and the zeta transform, which rely only on simple subtraction tricks via inclusion--exclusion (and does not even require fast Fourier transform), and so is conceptually easier to understand (the whole solution is about 5 pages long).
  2. Following a similar approach, we obtain a randomized algorithm for $k$-SUM for integer inputs for odd constant $k$ in $O(n^{\lceil k/2\rceil-\varepsilon_k})$ time for some constant $\varepsilon_k>0$, disproving the $k$-SUM Hypothesis for all odd $k$.
  3. Existing reductions from 3SUM and APSP to selected-entries rectangular matrix multiplication were randomized in the case of real-valued input. We present new deterministic reductions, yielding a truly subquadratic deterministic algorithm for Real 3SUM and a truly subcubic deterministic algorithm for Real APSP.

title: Asynchronous Flow Map Language Models
authors: Chanhyuk Lee, Wonjung Kim, Patrick Pynadath, Jaehoon Yoo, Satoshi Hayakawa, Ruqi Zhang, Jinwoo Kim, Seunghoon Hong
abstract: The order in which tokens are predicted in language modeling has a profound impact on the quality of generated sequences. Autoregressive and masked diffusion models iteratively fill in tokens and can exploit such orderings across generation steps, but how to leverage an ordering for one-step parallel language modeling is unclear. We introduce asynchronous flow map language models (aFMLMs), which incorporate prediction order into one-step modeling by learning the flow maps of asynchronous flows. These flows specify an ordering through a tokenwise time schedule that controls the relative denoising progress of tokens. We formulate a general class of asynchronous flows that admit both prescribed and learned, state-adaptive schedules, show that they define valid flow maps, and develop new methods for their flow map distillation. The resulting models can generate all tokens in a single forward pass by internalizing the ordering encoded in the flow into their hidden computations. On Sudoku solving and code generation for GSM8K math word problems, aFMLM establishes new state-of-the-art one-step performance.

title: When Does Jacobian Fine-Tuning Stabilize Neural PDE Emulators?
authors: Shreeyam Bangera, Manya Gupta
abstract: Neural emulators of chaotic PDEs are trained on one-step prediction but deployed autoregressively, where their errors compound. Jacobian-based regularisers aim to curb this growth, but in a chaotic system part of the growth is physical and cannot be trained away. We separate the two sources of this error with a first-order decomposition. We compare the emulator's error with a counterfactual that propagates the same one-step mistakes through the solver's Jacobian, giving an amplification ratio: the factor by which the model's own dynamics amplify its errors. We study 21 configurations across four PDEs, five architectures and two model sizes (8-10k and 33k parameters), with errors measured at one Lyapunov time. Jacobian fine-tuning reduced the error by more than 10% for 1 of 34 seeds whose amplification ratio was at most 1.25, and for all 20 seeds whose ratio was at least four; for the latter, the error fell by a factor of 8 (small models) and 55 (33k models) in geometric mean over seeds. The gain approximately equals the one-step accuracy cost of fine-tuning divided by the amplification ratio. Matching the solver's Jacobian along the model's own error direction (EDJM) outperformed random directions at the same cost on 28 of 35 seeds; input-noise injection performed comparably to EDJM.

title: Risk Assessment of Fair Multi-Period Dynamic Operating Envelopes under Uncertainty
authors: Pedro Salomão Quessongo, Daniel Gebbran, Wilhiam de Carvalho, Clodomiro Unsihuay-Vila
abstract: Dynamic operating envelopes (DOEs) can allocate time-varying export capacity to distributed energy resources (DERs), and while they are not intended to make operations immune to voltage violations, they should guide operations to mostly remain inside expected values under changing regimes and residual forecast errors. However, although recent literature proposed many different techniques for implementing DOEs, there is sparse discussion of analyzing and quantifying the risk of using more or less conservative DOEs under uncertain operating regimes. Having this gap in mind, this paper develops a risk-oriented extension of a previously established fair distributed multi-period optimal power flow (OPF) framework, where fair or technical DOEs are fixed as first-stage decisions and the OPF leverages battery energy storage and renewable curtailment as recourse under regime uncertainties. An independent nonlinear AC power flow then computes a resulting ensemble, which is summarized by (i) voltage-violation probability, severity, and a persistence metric for consecutive out-of-band hours, (ii) curtailment and Jain and Gini indices, and (iii) model deviations. Different probability situations are assessed, ranging from uniform, sunny-heavy, night-peak-heavy, and adversarial, which separate the envelope design from the assumed operating distribution. An optional outer loop allows for fine-tuning a fairness--efficiency parameter under explicit violation and persistence budgets. The combination of the outer loop and the overall framework, which quantifies how often and how severely operating limits are exceeded, creates an auditable methodology mixing equitable export allocation, distributed recourse, and AC risk assessment for active distribution network operators, and this framework is assessed using up to 1000 Monte Carlo scenarios per mixture and DOE design.

title: Nexus-VLA: Bridging Human and Robot Experiences via a Shared Hierarchical Semantic Latent Space
authors: Biaoliang Guan, Tingyu Yuan, Wen Ye, Ziming Ji, Xu Yang, Yan Huang, Jihua Zhu, Chaoyang Zhao
abstract: Large-scale egocentric human videos provide rich and scalable manipulation experience for robot policy learning, yet substantial embodiment gaps in visual appearance, kinematic structure, and action spaces hinder effective knowledge transfer. Existing methods often decouple cross-embodiment knowledge alignment from robot policy learning, making it difficult for human manipulation knowledge to directly and fully contribute to robot action learning. To address this issue, we propose Nexus-VLA, a hybrid policy learning framework that enables cross-embodiment knowledge transfer through end-to-end human-robot joint training, allowing human manipulation experience to directly contribute to robot policy learning. We first introduce a hierarchical cross-embodiment semantic alignment paradigm that progressively establishes shared manipulation semantics from task intent to fine-grained interactions, enabling more complete use of the manipulation knowledge contained in human videos. Building on this hierarchy, we design a shared manipulation latent representation that jointly encodes multi-level shared knowledge into an internal representation directly used for continuous action generation, improving policy learning efficiency while effectively leveraging human knowledge. Across RoboCasa-GR1, OOD settings, and real-world robot experiments, Nexus-VLA achieves an 80.5% task success rate on RoboCasa-GR1 and demonstrates strong advantages in human-data utilization, learning efficiency, and cross-scenario generalization.

title: Know When the Equation Is Wrong: Structural Uncertainty for LLM-Guided Symbolic Regression under Extrapolation
authors: Mostafa Cham, Bayu Adhi Tama, Jianwu Wang
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can help discover mathematical equations from data, but most LLM-guided symbolic regression methods focus on a single best equation without quantifying uncertainty over alternative functional forms. This is challenging because distinct equations can fit the observed data similarly while producing substantially different extrapolations. Our experiments on the LLM-SRBench dataset show that standard conformal intervals achieve nominal in-distribution coverage but frequently fail under extrapolation. To tackle this challenge, we introduce LLM-SR-UQ, a framework that retains competing equation structures and uses their disagreement to characterize uncertainty about the underlying functional form. We extend the standard fixed-width conformal approach to quantify structural intervals, which measure disagreement among candidate equations and identify where prediction intervals should widen. Extensive experiments show our framework substantially improves coverage attainment by incorporating structural disagreement while preserving in-distribution coverage. Our approach also shows good generalizability when it is applied to other symbolic-regression methods.

title: Capacity Meets the Four Subspace Problem: Distributed Linear Computation and the Cross-Ratio
authors: Hua Sun
abstract: $K$ users each observe a fixed linear function of common data over a finite field of characteristic $p$, and a server must recover another fixed linear function with zero error from one message sent by each user. The capacity, the minimum total number of symbols the users send per computed instance, depends only on the configuration of subspaces formed by these linear functions. We study the instance in which three users observe $\boldsymbol{a}$, $\boldsymbol{b}$ and $\boldsymbol{a}+\boldsymbol{b}$ and the server wants $\boldsymbol{a}+λ\boldsymbol{b}$. The four functions span four lines in a plane with cross-ratio $λ$, the smallest instance of the four subspace problem of representation theory. It is the smallest configuration whose capacity is not determined by the dimensions of the subspaces formed by sums and intersections: these dimensions are the same for every $λ$, but the capacity depends on the cross-ratio and on the prime subfield. For the harmonic cross-ratios, $λ=-1$, $λ=2$ or $2λ=1$, it is $2$: every zero-error code reveals $(\boldsymbol{a},\boldsymbol{b})$ to the server, so no code beats having two users send their observations. For $λ$ outside the prime subfield it is the cut-set bound $3/2$, achieved by codes linear over the prime subfield, while codes linear over the field need $2$. For the other $λ$ in the prime subfield it lies in $[3p/(2p-1),2]$, so no code at any block length approaches the cut-set bound. The qualitative separation persists under vanishing error for uniform data: the cut-set bound is tight exactly for $λ$ outside the prime subfield. The four-line instance is also exact repair of one node of a $[4,2]$ MDS storage code, and the results translate to that setting.

title: A Neural Network Approach towards Real-Time Knot Point Density Estimates for the Nonlinear Quadrotor
authors: Jasmine Ratchford, Raffaele Romagnoli, Mark H. Klein
abstract: Spline representations provide a compact way to approximate continuous trajectories using a finite number of parameters. When approximating trajectories generated by dynamical systems, the efficiency of a spline representation depends strongly on the placement of knot points. Uniform knot distributions often lead to inefficient representations, requiring either unnecessary control points or producing poor approximations in regions where the trajectory varies rapidly. In this work we propose a learning-based method for adaptive knot placement in B-spline approximations of trajectories generated by ordinary differential equations. A neural network learns a mapping from the initial condition of the system to quantities that characterize the local variation of the resulting trajectory. These estimates are used to construct nonuniform knot distributions that approximately equidistribute a local error indicator, reducing the number of control points needed to meet a prescribed accuracy.
comment: 8 pages, 5 figures. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible. This work is presented at IEEE CDC 2026

title: GhostPrefix: Synchronization-Free Universal Prefix Attacks for ASR Manipulation
authors: Shengding Liu, Ashwin Innuganti, Qiben Yan
abstract: We present GhostPrefix, the first synchronization-free universal adversarial prefix attack against automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems. Unlike prior audio attacks, which are typically crafted per utterance, require synchronization with the victim waveform, or target narrow objectives, GhostPrefix learns a short, reusable audio segment prepended to arbitrary live speech to exert real-time control over ASR outputs without knowledge of the future utterance or temporal alignment. A key challenge is maintaining stable adversarial effects across unknown, evolving speech contexts. GhostPrefix combines token-level losses with a novel representation-level objective for stable, input-agnostic effects. GhostPrefix supports three attack modes: (i) prompted prefix attacks for semantic steering, (ii) targeted prefix attacks for transcript hijacking, and (iii) untargeted prefix attacks for transcription degradation. To remain perceptually inconspicuous, we regularize prefixes toward benign environmental-sound distributions and improve robustness against over-the-air distortions. We evaluate GhostPrefix across 13 open-source ASR models from four families. In digital settings, it achieves average attack success rates of 97.6% for prompted steering and 93.4% for targeted hijacking, while driving word error rate to 1.18 under untargeted attacks. Over the air, it achieves success rates of 91.5% and 89.5% for prompted and targeted modes, respectively. These manipulations propagate into downstream AI-assisted pipelines, including voice assistants and AI note-taking tools, causing systematic semantic misinterpretations. GhostPrefix exposes synchronization-free universal prefixes as a practical, under-explored threat to real-world ASR and downstream applications. Artifacts and demos are available at https://ghostprefix.github.io/.

title: CausalXRL: Explainable Reinforcement Learning through Causal Graph Reasoning
authors: Yanming Zhang, Eric Papenhausen, Klaus Mueller
abstract: Reinforcement learning is a powerful paradigm for training autonomous agents and has achieved impressive performance in complex environments. However, this success often comes at the cost of interpretability, diminishing trust and complicating efforts to debug and improve agent behavior. To address these challenges, we introduce CausalXRL, a novel framework for explainable reinforcement learning (XRL). A key feature of CausalXRL is its use of causal graph reasoning, which provides transparent, structured, multi-level explanations of agent decision-making. We validate CausalXRL through comprehensive case studies and a two-part evaluation: (1) a quantitative analysis of explanation fidelity and causal-structure learning efficiency in benchmark RL environments, and (2) a qualitative expert study assessing explainability in the real-time strategy (RTS) benchmark MicroRTS. The quantitative results show that CausalXRL can provide faithful explanations while efficiently learning causal structures, and the qualitative expert study suggests that participants found CausalXRL useful for inspecting high-level RTS strategies.
